notices.title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source – HHS Modernization Discovery, Prototyping, and Implementation Planning
notices.agency_path: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF.OFFICE OF THE ASSISTANT SECRETARY FOR ADMINISTRATION (ASA)
notices.description_text:
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Office of the Assistant Secretary for Administration (ASA), Immediate Office (IO), intends to solicit and negotiate on a sole-source basis with YAT CHOI LLC for modernization discovery, prototyping, and implementation-planning services.

The Government anticipates conducting this acquisition using Simplified Acquisition Procedures under FAR Part 13. Pursuant to FAR 13.106-1(b)(1)(i), a contracting officer may solicit from one source for an acquisition not exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold when the circumstances of the contract action deem only one source reasonably available.

The anticipated award will be a firm-fixed-price contract valued at approximately $200,000, with a 25-week period of performance from September 30, 2026 through March 23, 2027. The requirement and pricing structure are reflected in the acquisition documentation currently provided by ASA.

Intended Source

YAT CHOI LLC

UEI: RT4EBWRLES43

CAGE Code: 22JT5

33 Greenwich Avenue, Apartment 10J

New York, NY 10014-2722

United States

YAT CHOI LLC maintains an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). Its current SAM registration expires July 3, 2027. The entity's SAM record includes NAICS 541512 and PSC DA01 among its registered service classifications.

Description of Requirement

HHS requires a senior-led modernization discovery, prototyping, and implementation-planning engagement for selected HHS programs, workflows, systems, and technical operations.

The engagement is intended to evaluate opportunities to improve organizational performance through business-process redesign, automation, artificial intelligence, improved data practices, and modern technical approaches. Existing processes may involve manual activities, fragmented workflows, repeated data entry, reconciliation, routing, review, and outdated technical tools.

The anticipated 25-week engagement consists of a five-week Mobilization and Readiness Phase, followed by a 20-week Discovery, Prototyping, and Implementation Planning Phase.

Mobilization and readiness activities are expected to include contractor staffing and onboarding; completion of applicable security, privacy, and system-access requirements; orientation to the HHS environment and selected systems; kickoff activities; and development of an integrated work plan.

Subsequent performance is expected to include discovery interviews and working sessions; review of selected workflows, systems, and technical operations; technical and process analysis; development and testing of prototypes or proofs of concept; validation with HHS stakeholders; and preparation of implementation recommendations and plans for opportunities selected by HHS.

Anticipated deliverables include:

 A current-state assessment;

 A prioritized modernization-opportunities portfolio evaluated for expected impact, feasibility, complexity, and time to value;

 Technical recommendations for high-priority opportunities;

 Agreed prototypes or proofs of concept;

 Implementation plans for opportunities or prototypes selected by HHS;

 Supporting technical and operational documentation;

 An implementation roadmap for remaining opportunities; and

 An executive readout or summary.

For HHS-selected prototypes, the contractor may also be required to provide applicable supporting technical artifacts, including source code, configuration files, data models and schemas, interface specifications, design documentation, build and testing instructions, and dependency or licensing information. These requirements are derived from the final Statement of Need.

Basis for Proposed Sole-Source Action

HHS considered whether full-service management consulting firms and other modernization providers could satisfy the requirement.

The Government's market research and source rationale found that conventional consulting firms generally would need to assemble a multidisciplinary team or obtain additional technical resources to provide the required combination of business-process modernization, artificial intelligence, automation, technical architecture, and rapid prototyping. Such an approach could introduce additional staffing, onboarding, coordination, and knowledge-transfer time within the required performance schedule.

YAT CHOI LLC has been identified as capable of providing the required management and technical capabilities through an integrated, senior-led engagement without reliance on multiple consulting teams or subcontracted technical specialists. The contemplated approach enables movement from discovery and process analysis to technical validation and prototyping within the required schedule.

The Government also anticipates use of a firm-fixed-price structure to establish price certainty and place responsibility on the contractor for delivery of the defined outcomes rather than reimbursement based on labor hours. The underlying source rationale is documented in the Statement of Need.

Classification

The Government anticipates classifying this acquisition under:

NAICS 541512 – Computer Systems Design Services

PSC DA01 – IT and Telecom – Business Application/Application Development Support Services (Labor)

The scope includes integrated systems and workflow analysis, modernization design, technical architecture, automation and AI-related technical work, prototype development and testing, and implementation planning. NAICS 541512 therefore best reflects the principal purpose of the acquisition.

YAT CHOI LLC's SAM registration separately confirms that it is registered under NAICS 541512 and PSC DA01. Under FAR 19.102, the appropriate NAICS classification is determined from the principal purpose of the Government requirement, including the solicitation description, function, and relative importance of its components.

Responses to This Notice

This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals or quotations and does not constitute a solicitation.

However, all responsible sources may submit a quotation or other written response demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Government's requirement. Timely responses will be considered by the Government in accordance with FAR 5.207. FAR 5.207 specifically requires a noncompetitive synopsis to identify the intended source and state the reason supporting the lack of competition.

Interested sources should provide sufficient information to allow HHS to evaluate whether the respondent possesses the technical, management, staffing, and organizational capabilities necessary to satisfy the requirement within the required schedule.

At a minimum, responses should include:

 Legal business name;

 Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code;

 Business size and socioeconomic status under NAICS 541512;

 Point-of-contact information;

 Relevant experience performing comparable modernization, systems-design, artificial-intelligence, automation, prototyping, and implementation-planning work;

 Description of the respondent's proposed technical and management approach;

 Identification of any subcontractors or additional technical resources required to perform the work;

 Ability to commence performance by the anticipated September 30, 2026 start date; and

 Sufficient pricing information for the Government to evaluate the response.

Responses must be submitted electronically no later than:

Tuesday September 15 at 4:00 PM EDT

to:

Mesfin Alemayehu

Contracting Officer

Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions

U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

mesfin.alemayehu@hhs.gov 

Telephone responses will not be accepted.

A determination by the Government regarding whether to compete the contemplated acquisition, based upon responses received to this notice, is within the discretion of the Government.

The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting information in response to this notice.

The purpose of this RFQ is to solicit quotes for Shure ANX4 Incremental Channel Expansion Licenses and UniFi Indoor Cat6A CMP cable for FEMA Region VI Federal Regional Center and the Texas Room located in the Russell Newman Building.

This is an open market RFQ under NAICS 541519, Other Computer Related Services, Information Technology Value Added Resellers, with a size standard of 150 employees. Award will be made on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) basis.

All licenses must be valid OEM or publisher-authorized entitlements. All cable supplies must be new, genuine OEM products. All quoted items must be TAA compliant, as applicable.

The range of affordability is $47,000.00. This amount is for affordability purposes only and is not a ceiling or floor.

Quoters shall provide an itemized quote for each CLIN, including product description, manufacturer, part number, quantity, unit price, extended price, and warranty or license support information.

Questions must be emailed to Destiny.Dyson@fema.dhs.gov by 12:00 PM CT on September 16, 2026. Quoters must reference RFQ 70FBR626Q00000041 in all correspondence. Phone calls will not be accepted.

Quotes must be emailed to Destiny.Dyson@fema.dhs.gov by 1:00 PM CT on September 22, 2026. Late quotes may not be considered.

Delivery shall occur within 65 calendar days after receipt of order. Invoices may be submitted only after all required items and license/support information have been delivered and accepted by the Government.

The nonmanufacturer rule is not separately stated in the RFQ. The Government confirms that the nonmanufacturer rule does not apply to this acquisition because the RFQ is at or below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold. All other terms and conditions of the RFQ remain unchanged, including the requirements for new, genuine OEM products and valid publisher-authorized license entitlements, authorized reseller or distributor documentation, delivery, warranty/support, and all applicable RFQ requirements.

A non-TAA country of origin, by itself, will not make a CLIN technically unacceptable, provided the quoted item otherwise meets all RFQ requirements, including requirements for new, genuine, authorized, non-counterfeit, non-gray-market products and valid license entitlements. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged.

The Department of Homeland Security, Federal Emergency Management Agency, has identified a need to replace end-of-life laptops and acquire various IT peripheral equipment necessary to maintain operational capability, cybersecurity compliance, and workforce productivity.

The purpose of this Request for Quotation is to solicit quotations from authorized resellers and distributors for the supply of the brand-name equipment identified in the schedule of supplies, including Dell, Cisco, Samsung, Sharp, Crestron, and associated peripheral equipment.

This RFQ is issued as an open market total small business set-aside under NAICS 541519, Other Computer Related Services, with a small business size standard of $34.0 million. Award will be made to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable responsible small business quoter whose quotation conforms to all requirements of this RFQ.

The Product Service Code for this requirement is 7B22, IT and Telecom, Compute: Servers, Storage, and Components.

Offerors shall identify the exact brand name, model number, part number, and specifications of each item proposed. All quoted items must match the specified brand name, model number, part number, and configuration exactly. Substitutions, alternatives, or deviations will not be accepted unless expressly authorized in writing by the Contracting Officer.

Offerors must be authorized resellers or distributors of the specified brands. The Government reserves the right to verify reseller or distributor authorization directly with the original equipment manufacturer. Offerors shall provide a letter or certificate of authorization upon request.

The Government seeks quotes with a total price less than $327,000.00. Quoters should not interpret this figure as a ceiling or as a floor on offers. This information is provided as a courtesy to prospective offerors. The Government may select an offer for award with a price below, at, or exceeding this figure if it finds the quotation technically acceptable, price is reasonable, and funds are available.

Delivery shall be FOB Destination. Equipment shall be delivered within 70 calendar days after receipt of order. Shipment tracking information and delivery confirmation shall be provided upon request.

All questions and quotations shall be submitted by email to the Contracting Officer, Destiny Dyson, at Destiny.Dyson@fema.dhs.gov. Phone calls will not be accepted.

Quoters shall use the following identifier on all correspondence:

Open Market RFQ 70FBR626Q00000043 - FEMA Region VI IT Equipment

Questions regarding this RFQ are due no later than September 17, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central Time. Questions shall be submitted by email to the Contracting Officer, Destiny Dyson, at Destiny.Dyson@fema.dhs.gov. Questions submitted after the deadline may not be answered. Oral questions or responses are not binding. Only written responses issued by the Contracting Officer are binding on the Government.

Quotations are due no later than September 23, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central Time. Quotations shall be submitted by email to the Contracting Officer, Destiny Dyson, at Destiny.Dyson@fema.dhs.gov. Quotations submitted by any other method may not be considered unless expressly authorized by the Contracting Officer.

Quoters are responsible for ensuring that quotations are received by the Contracting Officer by the due date and time. Late quotations may not be considered in accordance with applicable procedures.

Quotations shall remain valid for 30 calendar days from the quotation due date.

Delivery Address: FEMA Region VI Federal Regional Center 800 North Loop 288 Denton, Texas 76209

notices.title: Microsoft 365 Data Migration Project
notices.agency_path: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.SSP.STRATEGIC WEAPONS FAC PAC FINANCIAL
notices.description_text:
Statement of Work

Microsoft 365 Project

1. Background

Strategic Weapons Facility Pacific (SWFPAC) currently supports a legacy Microsoft Access 2003 database identified as mission-critical and in need of immediate migration. This system serves as a warehouse and inventory management solution tracking defined storage locations, personnel assignments, and two distinct categories of inventory. SWFPAC requires professional services to facilitate the migration of mission-critical data from the Access legacy database to Flank Speed, ensuring compatibility and interoperability with the Navy enterprise with minimal disruption to SWFPAC operations.

2. Scope of Work

The vendor shall provide all necessary personnel, expertise, and services to design and build an application compatible with the Navy's Microsoft 365 platform (often referred to ask "Flank Speed") to facilitate the migration of data from an existing Microsoft Access 2003 database to Flank Speed. The final product will utilize SharePoint Online (SPO) as the primary data repository and Microsoft Power Platform (Power Apps and Power Automate) for user interfaces, relational workflows, and automated document generation.

2.1 Vendor Competency Requirements

Interested vendors must provide documented evidence of successful past performance and technical competency in designing, deploying, and supporting migrations from legacy Microsoft Access systems to Microsoft 365/Power Platform environments.

2.2 Data Architecture, Test Environment, & Migration Support

Due to data security protocols, the vendor will not be provided access to live data. Instead of dictating a rigid target architecture, the Government requires the vendor to evaluate the legacy Access 2003 database structure and propose an optimized target architecture.

The vendor's proposed data schema must successfully manage and relate the following core situational entities (encompassing datasets that range from <500 up to 3,000 records):

Warehouse Locations (Racks/Lockers)

Defined physical locations that can be assigned inventory, and subsequently assigned/issued to specific personnel.

Personnel Assignments

Tracking individuals assigned to specific racks, lockers, or individual pieces of equipment (handling check-in, check-out, and return states).

General Gear Inventory

Non-serialized bulk items categorized and inventoried by aggregates (tracking total quantities, quantities assigned out, and available quantities remaining).

Serialized Gear Inventory

Individually tracked items where inventory, historical status, and assignments are maintained by individual unit (serial number), distinctly from general gear.

The Vendor is expected to design and implement the most efficient, scalable SPO data schema necessary to deliver a fully functional solution handling these relationships, which may include core tables, lookup lists, workflow state management, and archives. The architecture must support full data lifecycle management, ensuring that inactive core records (e.g., separated personnel, retired inventory) can be archived and removed from active views, but securely maintained for a specified timeframe to meet audit requirements prior to permanent deletion.

Once the design is approved, the vendor shall construct the architecture and populate it with synthetic test data to enable rigorous User Acceptance Testing (UAT). The vendor must facilitate testing cycles, incorporate feedback, and perform any necessary reworks identified by the internal team to guarantee the solution's full operability and alignment with mission requirements. The Vendor will provide structural templates and technical guidance to the internal team. The internal team will be solely responsible for the extraction, transformation, and loading of the live Access 2003 data into the new platform.

2.3 Application, Workflow, & Security Scope 

 

Using the synthetic test data, the vendor shall develop and refine through repeat testing a unified Power Apps interface and Power Automate workflows to handle relational data linking (e.g., assigning inventory to racks, and issuing racks/inventory to personnel), automated document generation, approval routing, and comprehensive transaction logging. Forms and transaction logs must be automatically routed to designated SPO Document Libraries. Throughout the solution's development, the Vendor shall facilitate discussions with the SWFPAC internal team to define, configure, and enforce appropriate permission restrictions and user groupings across all system components (SPO Lists, Document Libraries, and Power Platform interfaces).

3. Deliverables

The vendor shall provide the following deliverables according to the agreed-upon project schedule.

Title

Description & Acceptance Criteria

D.1

System Architecture & Design Plan

A comprehensive design document outlining the proposed SPO data schema. The design must ensure all core entities effectively correlate, support multiple identifying columns per entity, and detail the document library structure and proposed permission groupings/restrictions. The System Architecture and Design Plan must be approved by the Government POC prior to development.

D.2

SPO Infrastructure & Migration Support Guide

Construction of the approved SPO data architecture populated with vendor-generated test data. Delivery of a Migration Guide providing the SWFPAC internal team with step-by-step instructions and support mechanisms for executing the live data transfer.

D.3

Data Entry & Management Interface

A Power App (or customized SPO form interface) validated with test data and refined via internal team feedback, enabling users to securely add, view, edit, and archive entries across all migrated datasets. The interface must support capturing multiple identifying columns (including serial numbers where applicable) for each entity, maintain effective relational correlations, and provide adaptable sorting/filtering views for easy data retrieval during audits. Access and editing capabilities must be strictly locked down by approved permission groupings to prevent unauthorized or erroneous changes.

D.4

Relational Assignment Workflows

Power Automate flows enabling users to create, manage, and track relational assignments (e.g., assigning specific gear to racks/lockers, and issuing inventory/racks to personnel). Workflows must govern the full check-in, check-out, and return lifecycle, and must include data validation logic and permission lock-downs to prevent erroneous correlations or improper inventory adjustments.

D.5

Approval Routing Workflows

Automated workflows requiring designated approvals for specific assignment transactions to ensure accountability. Must include notification mechanisms.

D.6

Automated & Manual Document Generation

System capability to generate two (2) distinct types of templated documents based on list data and assignment conditions. Must include both an automatic trigger (condition-based) and a manual prompt option.

D.7

Document Library Configuration

Setup of three (3) distinct SPO Document Libraries: Two for storing the documents generated in D.6, and one for the transaction logs in D.8. Access must be restricted based on defined user groupings.

D.8

Transaction Logging, Audit Views & Comprehensive Archival

An automated logging mechanism capturing a comprehensive change history (all system changes, relational connections, check-in/out transactions, and edits) with users and timestamps identified. Logs must be locked down via permissions to prevent tampering. The system must support the secure archiving of historical transactional data as well as inactive core records (e.g., personnel, inventory), maintaining them for a designated timeframe to satisfy audit requirements before permanent removal. It must also provide adaptable list views for authorized users to retrieve and review ad-hoc audit data, and automatically generate and export an Excel format transaction report on a monthly cadence to a dedicated Document Library.

D.9

As-Built Architecture Documentation

Final, comprehensive documentation detailing the deployed solution, list schemas, flow logic, implemented permission restrictions/groupings, archival/retention logic, and maintenance requirements.

D.10

Knowledge Transfer & Handoff

A dedicated training session (and accompanying materials) for internal developers covering system maintenance, future minor edits, and active support during the internal team's live data migration phase.

4.0 Place of Performance The place of performance shall be 100% remote at the Vendor's facility. No on-site travel, base access, or physical presence at Strategic Weapons Facility Pacific (SWFPAC) is required or authorized.

5.0 Period of Performance The Period of Performance (PoP) for this effort shall be 180 calendar days from the date of contract award.

6.0 Security: All data exported from the SWFPAC environment will be scrubbed of any Controlled Unclassified Information by SWFPAC personnel prior to vendor receipt of data.

notices.title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE:Law Manager Software License, Maintenance, and Technical Support Services
notices.agency_path: HOMELAND SECURITY, DEPARTMENT OF.US COAST GUARD.HQ CONTRACT OPERATIONS (CG-912)(000
notices.description_text:
1. INTRODUCTION & STATUTORY AUTHORITY

The United States Coast Guard (USCG), Headquarters Contract Division 4 (CG-HCA-COCO-41), on behalf of the Office of Legal Policy and Program Development (USCG-LPD), intends to negotiate on a sole-source basis with Mitratech, located in Conshohocken, PA.

The proposed contract action is to acquire proprietary software licenses, custom support services, ongoing maintenance, and upgrades for the Law Manager software application.

The Government intends to solicit and negotiate this requirement under the statutory authority of:

 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1) or 41 U.S.C. 253(c)(1), as implemented by FAR Subpart 6.302-1(a)(2)(iii): "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements."

This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency.

2. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT

The USCG Office of Legal Policy and Program Development (USCG-LPD) has a continuous, mission-critical requirement to obtain technical support services, maintenance support, software upgrades, and application modifications for the Law Manager software. Law Manager serves as the primary system of record and workload repository for approximately 300+ Coast Guard Legal Program personnel across Coast Guard Headquarters, ten District legal offices, several base legal offices, the Office of Physical Disability Evaluations, and their respective clients.

Key System Specifications & Structure

The Law Manager system comprises six main notebooks/tabs used for tracking, docketing, and case management across all USCG legal practice areas:

 Entity: Tracks units and individuals associated with cases (witnesses, counsel, judges, experts, plaintiffs, defendants).

 Matter: Handles legal assistance files and general legal inquiries.

 Military Justice: Manages military justice actions (e.g., courts-martial) and calculates the Speedy Trial Clock fields based on charges and calendars.

 Physical Disability (PDES): Evaluates cases for personnel seeking disability benefits.

 Regulations: Tracks the drafting, clearance, and review of regulatory documents.

 Claims/Litigation: Tracks affirmative and defensive claims and litigation for or against the USCG.

The software is accessed via both a heavy client-installed application (for bulk data entry and speed) and a secure web application (primarily for reservists and personnel outside the Coast Guard Data Network).

Scope of Work & Deliverables

The contractor will be responsible for the following core tasks:

 Ongoing Maintenance & Technical Support: Deliver modified production code, technical documentation, operational procedures, and product updates to ensure zero-error system performance during normal business hours.

 System Configuration & Custom Modifications: Assist with minor configuration changes (e.g., adding/removing fields, re-labeling existing fields, enhancing functionality as the application-image evolves).

 Software Upgrades & Security Patches: Provide and assist in the installation of all software upgrades, tool sets, and database environment updates.

 Testing: Develop Conformance Acceptance Testing (CAT) plans and run verification test scripts with mock data for adding, updating, finding, and deleting records within all system notebooks.

 Optional Report Writing Tool (Section 2.3.1): Acquire a fully compatible, vendor-supported ad hoc report writing and querying tool.

 Optional Support Hours (Section 2.3.2): Secure up to 1,000 hours of custom technical support to execute USCG-specific modifications.

3. ESTIMATED VALUE & PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE

The Government anticipates awarding a Fixed Price contract with an estimated total value of $828,845 covering a one (1) year base period and four (4) consecutive one-year option periods:

Base Year

Period of Performance

Start Date: September 30, 2026

End Date September 29, 2027

Option Year 1

September 30, 2027-

September 29, 2028

Option Year 2

September 30, 2028-

September 29, 2029

Option Year 3

September 30, 2029-

September 29, 2030

Option Year 4

 September 30, 2030-

September 29, 2031

4. SOLE SOURCE DETERMINATION RATIONALE

The Law Manager application is a highly customized, proprietary commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software system. Mitratech is the developer, sole intellectual property owner, and original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of Law Manager.

The justification for sole-source award to Mitratech is based on the following critical technical factors:

 Access to Source Code & Engineers: Mitratech has sole access to the software engineers who created Law Manager and is the only entity that can resolve deep-level software bugs or configure the application to integrate smoothly with the Coast Guard's standard operating image. Mitratech personnel possess exclusive access to the proprietary source code for current and future releases.

 Proprietary Technical Documentation: Mitratech personnel utilize proprietary technical documentation and receive unique, specialized internal training/briefings directly from the Law Manager product development team that are unavailable to any third party.

 Restricted Licensing Policy: Mitratech does not re-license its maintenance agreements for upgrades. No other vendor in the market owns the rights or data to Thomson Elite's original source code or Mitratech's proprietary assets.

 Mission Criticality: This software is vital to daily USCG legal operations. Specifically, attorneys must perform immediate, reliable conflict-of-interest checks within the Law Manager database before consulting with clients. It is also the sole vehicle for workload metrics and resource allocation reporting at Coast Guard Headquarters.

 Significant Cost & Legacy History: In 1999, the Coast Guard abandoned its efforts to migrate mission-critical applications from legacy CTOS to Windows due to database porting failures. After a rigorous selection process, the USCG selected and deployed Law Manager in 2001. A replacement effort would lead to a massive duplication of costs (including a minimum of $828,845 in support, plus undocumented system engineering, data migration, and extensive staff retraining costs) and severe, unacceptable operational disruptions that are impossible to recover through competition.

5. SUBMISSION OF CAPABILITY STATEMENTS

Interested firms who believe they can fully meet the Government's requirement may submit a capability statement. Because Mitratech does not re-license its maintenance agreements or share its proprietary source code, any responding firm must provide clear, undeniable written proof of their legal right, authorized partner status, and independent capability to modify and upgrade the Law Manager application without voiding current licensing, warranties, or security configurations.

At a minimum, responses must include:

 Company Profile: Name, physical address, Point of Contact (POC), UEI number, Cage Code, and business size under NAICS 541519.

 Authorized Documentation: Written authorization directly from the OEM (Mitratech) confirming the respondent has full access to, and authority to edit, the proprietary source code and technical documentation.

 Staffing Qualifications: Demonstration of qualified personnel (e.g., Project Manager) available during standard business hours (0800–1600 EST) to meet all SOW requirements.

 Technical Qualifications: A detailed description of the firm's experience supporting Law Manager platforms within the federal sector.

 Staffing Capabilities: Evidence of qualified personnel (such as a Project Manager meeting the SOW standard of M-F, 0800-1600 EST availability) capable of managing the transition, Conformance Acceptance Testing (CAT), and custom programming requirements.

Capability statements must be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist listed below no later than September 14, 2026, 3:00 PM EST.

notices.title: Medical Records Coding Software for the Cass Lake Service Unit
notices.agency_path: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF.INDIAN HEALTH SERVICE.BEMIDJI SUB-AREA,
notices.description_text:
NOTICE OF INTENT TO ISSUE SOLE SOURCE AWARD

The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Indian Health Service (IHS), Bemidji Area intends to award a Firm Fixed Priced Contract on a sole source basis to Solventum Health Information Systems, Inc. for Cass Lake Indian Hospital, Cass Lake, MN. The anticipated period of performance will be a Base plus 4 Option Years.

This Intent to Sole Source is in accordance with FAR Part 12 Acquisition of Commercial Items. Under the authority of FAR 6.302-1, only one responsible source and no other will satisfy agency requirements, the Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed price Sole Source contract to Solventum as only one source reasonably available.

Solventum Health Information Systems encoding software is unique in that it contains both ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes. CLSU has used Solventum encoding software for more than a decade because of its unique qualities and efficiencies. Market Research has determined that other vendors offer coding software, but do not have the ability to interface with the IHS Resource Patient Management system which we are mandated to use. The price of the software has decreased while staff productivity increases through utilization of this product in comparison to using a standard codebook. Solventum encoding software includes many coding reference materials, which saves the CLSU from purchasing reference books. Solventum has extensive experience with encoding software and software support. Coding staff at the CLSU are highly trained in utilizing the Solventum encoding system.

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541519, Other Computer Related Services with a size standard of 34 Million.

Point of contact for this acquisition is Contract Specialist Mary Simon, mary.simon2@ihs.gov. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes. Interested persons may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit a quote to Contract Specialist Mary Simon, mary.simon2@ihs.gov.

Information received in response to this notice will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. 

Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. In doing so, interested sources must submit technical capabilities, and other information that demonstrates their ability to meet the Government's needs.

The STVHCS currently has 6 Pathologists, 2 Surgical Residents, 1 Hematology Fellow, 1 Grossing Technician dictating gross and microscopic descriptions into the dictation system. Dictations can be routed to in-house transcriptionists for typing and reporting in Vista for the user to review and make suggestions for any changes before signoff.

 Structured document templates via the VoiceOver Pro report builder.

 Free-text dictation or report information

 Ability to provide shared(departmental)templates in addition to personal templates per pathologist

 The VoiceOver Pro software also incorporates College of American Pathology cancer protocol checklists that are required by Commission on Cancer guidelines.

notices.description_text:
The procedures outlined in this CSO apply to Areas of Interest posted under W50NH9-26-S-0001.

NOTE: Proposed Solutions that may meet the needs of other Federal Agencies may be shared, as appropriate.

This announcement serves as the Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) for the Army Intelligence Enterprise- Information Technology Services (AIE-ITS), issued by Army Contracting Command – Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA) under solicitation W50NH9-26-S-0001. The objective of this CSO is to leverage agile acquisition authorities to enhance, secure, sustain, and modernize the global Information Technology (IT) environment supporting Army Intelligence operations across Continental United States (CONUS) and Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS) locations at the Project, Activity, or Enterprise scale. By lowering barriers to entry for commercial innovators, small businesses, and nontraditional defense contractors, the Government seeks best-of-breed solutions that transition the enterprise away from rigid, labor-hour execution toward outcome-oriented service delivery. This CSO will remain open until September 11, 2036.

The CSO operates under a strict Dual-Track architecture:

Track 1: General Submissions (Continuously Open). Vendors may submit written Solution Briefs (White Papers) at any time against the Open Areas of Interest (AoIs) outlined in Section 9.0 of the attached CSO document.

Track 2: Calls for Innovative Solutions (Targeted Closed Deadlines). The Government will periodically issue targeted, "Calls for Innovative Solutions" addressing specific Closed Areas of Interest. These notices will be published via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module with concurrent notices posted to SAM.gov. Vendors responding to a targeted Call must adhere strictly to the specific instructions, formats, and closing deadlines specified within that closed AOI. Late submissions will be rejected.

The competitive process under this CSO will generally follow a streamlined, multi-phased evaluation approach: Phase 1 (Submission of Written Solution Brief), Phase 2 (Presentation/Pitch, if applicable), and Phase 3 (Request for Commercial Solution Proposal). Resulting awards may include FAR Part 12 Fixed-Price contracts or non-FAR agreements. The Government will not reimburse companies for costs associated with developing submissions.

For complete details, the full CSO document is provided in the attachments. Please review the attached file, which describes all requirements, evaluation factors, and other pertinent information governing this solicitation.

notices.description_text:
DCSA INNOVATION GATEWAY

INNOVATION CALL #01

Unified Application Access and Integration Prototype

This is Innovation Call #01 under the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) Innovation Gateway (HS0021-26-CSO-DCSA).

Requirement Title

Unified Application Access and Integration Prototype

Problem Statement

DCSA's mission operations for personnel vetting, industrial security, counterintelligence, and insider-threat activities are supported by multiple separate applications that users must navigate to complete related work. This fragmented environment creates disconnected workflows, inconsistent authentication and user experiences, and inefficient access paths that increase user burden and reduce operational efficiency. It also adds complexity to the sustainment, modification, and modernization of mission applications and services.

DCSA requires a more unified and user-centered approach that improves workflow continuity and usability while preserving continuity of operations for existing Individual Engagement (IE) applications during prototype development and evaluation. The underlying challenge is to transition from siloed legacy capabilities to an integrated platform of modular components that can support phased integration, replacement, and modernization of back-end services without disrupting the user experience or mission execution.

KEY DATES

 Innovation Call Posting: 09/10/2026

 Questions Due Date: 09/14/2026 @ 11:00am ET

 Live Q&A Session: 09/16/2026 @ 11:00am ET

 Solution Concept Paper Due Date: 09/18/2026 @ 9:00am ET

 Estimated Period of Performance Start: 10/15/2026

Points of Contact (POC)

Please send all questions and submissions via email to the following POCs:

Agreements Officer (AO): Daniela Garavito, daniela.garavito2.civ@mail.mil

Agreements Specialist (AS): Salima McCravey, salima.a.mccravey.civ@mail.mil

Use the following email subjects for your email correspondence: 

Q&A: "DCSA – Innovation Call #01 – Q&A - [insert Company Name]"

Solution Concept Paper: "DCSA – Innovation Call #01 – Concept Paper [insert Company Name]"

Notice to Vendors

Further information on this requirement can be found in the attachments to this posting.

For instructions on submission of Solution Concept Papers and Full Project Proposals, please review the DCSA Innovation Gateway (HS0021-26-CSO-DCSA) general solicitation.

notices.title: Firewall Security Management Tool Tufin Support
notices.agency_path: TREASURY, DEPARTMENT OF THE.INTERNAL REVENUE SERVICE.IT STRATEGY AND MODERNIZATION
notices.description_text:
The primary purpose of this request is to procure the Tufin Enterprise Suite. Tufin will support the Common Communications Gateway (CCG) and CSRIC/Cybersecurity teams in reviewing,analyzing, auditing, and implementing firewall policy changes. It will replace the FireMon Security Manager, streamlining policy management and change workflows.

The platform integrates with enforcement points—including firewalls, routers, cloud accounts, and SASE services—via API and CLI access to retrieve live configurations and routing data. This capability enables Tufin to generate an interactive, unified map that consolidates traffic flows, endpoints, and connectivity paths across hybrid environments.

Tufin provides comprehensive Security Policy Management capabilities, including change tracking, policy optimization and cleanup, device configuration compliance and audit, and network segmentation management. It enhances network visibility through detailed mapping, visualization, and path analysis to support efficient troubleshooting and operational insight. Additionally, Tufin integrates with ServiceNow to support ITSM change management processes. This integration enables automation of key functions such as proactive risk assessment, change request verification, change design and path identification, and target selection, streamlining workflow efficiency and reducing manual intervention.

notices.description_text:
***Update 10 Sept: Q&A has been provided via excel attachment. No further questions will be considered. Submission Deadline: Whitepapers must be submitted via email to Katelyn O'Connor, katelyn.j.oconnor.civ@health.mil and Jena Bowman, jena.l.bowman.civ@health.mil no later than September 14, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT. Submissions received after this date and time will not be considered.

**Update 9 Sept: Q&A will be posted by COB 10 Sept. Attachment EUS_AOI1_AWACS_090926 has been updated.

PAE MDS is interested in awarding FAR-based Contract (e.g., FAR Part 12) or Prototype Project Other Transaction Agreement (pOTA) under 10 U.S.C. § 4022. Anticipate a 12-month base plus 4 12-month options for this AOI. AOI #1 AWACS leverages the competitive process under DHA Enterprise-Wide Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) HT003826SC005, https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/cd16b90540b7407fb4de1e028cea74d4/view 

Opportunity Overview:

To maximize the value of the Department's health technology investments, PAE MDS is transitioning from legacy, labor-intensive support contracts to a unified, outcome-based EUS delivery model.

Success in the EUS environment depends on delivering services precisely tailored to diverse user communities. A one-size-fits-all support model is unacceptable. The EUS ecosystem supports 11 distinct User Domains, ranging from point-of-care clinicians in garrison, to operational combat medics in disconnected environments, to the beneficiaries accessing the patient portal, as well as the highly specialized System Administrators, Biomedical Engineers, and local Information Technology (IT) support personnel who maintain these environments. Proposed solutions must demonstrate the flexibility to accommodate the unique workflows, priorities, and connectivity constraints of these diverse groups. This includes the inherent scalability to absorb new federal partners, seamlessly adapt enterprise workflows (e.g., MEPCOM), and tailor enablement materials for diverse components (e.g., National Guard) as the PAE MDS product ecosystem expands. While this AoI supports Defense Health Agency (DHA) and Military Service staff who interact with beneficiaries (the 11th User Domain), this AoI explicitly excludes a request to address direct, patient-facing digital engagement, which is reserved for Pillar 8 and may be addressed in a future AoI.

The total EUS ecosystem is structured around eight integrated Service Pillars:

 Service Desk & Information Technology Service Management (ITSM)

 Application & Clinical Workflow Support (Focus of this AoI)

 Enablement & Adoption Services (Focus of this AoI)

 Disconnected Enabler

 Change, Communications, & Trust (Focus of this AoI)

 Service Intelligence & Governance Support

 Program Management & Service Integration

 Beneficiary Digital Experience

While this specific AoI focuses exclusively on transforming and integrating Pillars 2, 3, and 5, Offerors must understand that these pillars do not operate in a silo. Any IT solution, automated framework, or workflow compliance strategy proposed under this AoI must be designed to seamlessly integrate with the broader EUS ecosystem, specifically, passing data to the enterprise ITSM Service Desk (Pillar 1) and supporting the overarching Government Service Integration and Management (SIAM) processes and integration authorities.

Questions: Must be submitted via email to the POCs listed below no later than September 2, 2026, at 11:00 AM EDT. Answers will be posted collectively on SAM.gov no later than close of business (COB) on September 10, 2026. Questions received after September 2, 2026 11:00AM EDT will not be considered. 

Submission Deadline: Whitepapers must be submitted via email to Katelyn O'Connor, katelyn.j.oconnor.civ@health.mil and Jena Bowman, jena.l.bowman.civ@health.mil no later than September 14, 2026, at 5:00 PM EDT. Submissions received after this date and time will not be considered.

Cost of Preparation: Per the CSO terms, the Government is not liable for any costs associated with the preparation of materials submitted in response to this AOI.

Important Instructions for Interested Parties: Interested parties are strongly encouraged to review the attached documents in their entirety for complete details regarding this opportunity, including submission requirements and other specific instructions.

notices.description_text:
The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) Innovation Gateway is a competitive solicitation that will result in the award of prototype projects under Other Transaction Agreements (OTA).

It is our commercially-focused front door for innovators.

Our goal is simple: to partner with creative companies to solve our most critical mission challenges.

Innovation Gateway Process

The Innovation Gateway is a general announcement of DCSA's general areas of interest (Digital Transformation Enablement, Data Integration and Advanced Analytics, Cyber and Industrial Security, Digital Workforce and Governance). The general soliciation includes criteria for selecting Solution Concept Papers and soliciting the participation of all proposers capable of satisfying the Government's needs.

Proposal requests will be issued via 'Innovation Calls' that are published separately under the DCSA Innovation Gateway at various times during the open period of this solicitation. 

Innovation Calls will be published via Sam.gov through separate solicitation postings referencing the DCSA Innovation Gateway. Proposers are required to use the Solution Concept Paper Template (DCSA Innovation Gateway Attachment 1) to submit their solutions.

The Government will only accept proposals in response to Innovation Calls. Unsolicited proposals that are not in response to an Innovation Call will not be reviewed by the Government. The Defense Health Agency (DHA) intends to negotiate a sole source contract under the authority of FAR § 12.102(a) and 41 U.S.C. 3304 with Abbott Rapid Diagnostics Informatics, Inc. notices.title: COMBINED PRE-SOLICITATION SYNOPSIS AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD  A SOLE-SOURCE CONTRACT: 5-year IDIQ/Enterprise Contract for Everfox Software Licenses, Maintenance and Support Services
notices.agency_path: DEPT OF DEFENSE
notices.description_text:
COMBINED PRE-SOLICITATION SYNOPSIS AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD

A SOLE-SOURCE CONTRACT (COMMERCIAL OFF-THE-SHELF EVERSOFT SOFTWARE) FAR Part 12

This special notice meets posting requirements of RFO FAR 5.1, 6.1, 12.1 and DFARS 206.3. It also serves as market research pursuant to RFO FAR 10.

The Government intends to award a 5-year, sole-source, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ)/Enterprise Contract (EC) with the first order to be issued prior to the conclusion of Fiscal Year 2026.

Anticipated Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP)

Intended Sole Source OEM: Everfox (https://www.everfox.com/)

Estimated Contract Ceiling: $75M-$90M

This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a quotation, which shall be considered by the agency.

DESCRIPTION OF REQUIRED SUPPLIES AND SERVICES

The Government has an ongoing operational requirement to procure enterprise-level, commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software licenses, specialized hardware appliances, hardware/software maintenance, and engineering support services provided by Everfox. (or brand-name equivalent solutions satisfying all salient characteristics)

The requirement encompasses a 5-year Ordering Period. Specific part numbers, nomenclature, and projected annual quantities across the total ordering period are itemized in the attached spreadsheet ("Attachment 1 - Requirements Listing").

The required supplies and services are categorized across three core areas:

A. SOFTWARE LICENSES, SUBSCRIPTIONS, AND MAINTENANCE

 Cross-Domain Guards: Perpetual and subscription licenses, standard maintenance, and associated filter bundles for Structured Guard (2070 Series), Unstructured Guard (2068 Series), and High-Speed Guard (2071 Series) supporting multi-network data transfer.

 Centralized Management & Endpoint Access: Control Center Server and Managed Device subscriptions (CCMDS/CCSVS Series) and Trusted Thin Client (TTC) Distribution Console, End User Device (EUD), and Network Resource licenses (10251 Series).

 Collaboration & Security Plugins: Everfox Information eXchange (DSIXTL1PU), Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Extended Lifecycle Support (ELS) nodes, and McAfee-integrated Virus Scanning Plug-Ins (2070VSP Series).

 Form, Fit, and Function: Software must execute native cross-domain security filtering and multi-level desktop access without requiring modification to existing agency security classification boundary policies.

B. HARDWARE APPLIANCES AND HARDWARE MAINTENANCE

 Data Diode Appliances: Fiber-optic hardware-enforced one-way data transfer appliances (FDD10G Series) including annual hardware warranty and associated software maintenance.

 Cross-Domain Access (CDA) & Verifier Hardware: G2CI Cross Domain Access V2 custom hardware and hardware maintenance (1079H-CDA Series) and High-Speed Verifier turnkey appliances (HSVT Series).

 Form, Fit, and Function: Hardware units must conform to standard 19-inch rack-mount form factors, interface with existing fiber-optic distribution fabrics, and satisfy DoD physical separation and emissions containment standards.

C. SPECIALIZED ENGINEERING AND TECHNICAL SERVICES

 Direct Tier-3/4 Engineering Support: Dedicated Junior, Mid-level, and Senior Product Engineers (5000/5001/5002-CDA Series) possessing relevant security clearances to provide on-site/remote deployment, complex troubleshooting, and integration.

 Training and Operational Travel: Basic and advanced CDA system administration training (40003-CDA Series) and associated travel (PS-TRAV-CDA) in support of mission locations.

All responsible sources—including OEM-authorized commercial resellers and distributors—may submit a quote for the exact products (or brand-name equivalents) and quantities listed in Attachment 1.

If submitting a quote for brand name equivalents, your quote must be supported by a capability statement (3-page limit, 11 pt. font) and a crosswalk of proposed alternatives to the requirements listed herein.

Quoted Pricing Submission Requirements:

 Pricing must be separated by year

 Each line item must include Part Number, Product Description, PoP, Type, unit pricing and extended pricing

 Any additional fees

Attach the End User License Agreement (EULA)/ End User Service Agreement (EUSA) and include a statement of understanding that the attached addendum (Attachment 2 – Federal SLA Addendum) or one patently similar (and approved by the Contracting Officer after legal review) MUST be signed by the OEM prior to award.

notices.title: Wideband Remote Monitoring Sensor (WRMS) Enhancement and Sustainment (E&S)
notices.agency_path: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEFENSE INFORMATION SYSTEMS AGENCY (DISA).IT CONTRACTING DIVISION - PL83
notices.description_text:
This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to determine the availability and technical capability of small and large businesses to provide the required products and/or services.

The WRMS E&S requirement falls under Project Officer Wideband Control as part of its mission to acquire and install state-of-the-art strategic satellite network control and planning systems for use with the Defense Satellite Communications System and Wideband Global Satellite Communications (WGS), and to provide satellite monitoring in either synchronized Spectrum Information Gathering or In-beam monitoring modes.

At its most basic level, the primary function of WRMS is to aid the user with the identification and resolution of anomalies detected by the system. Anomalies are presented to the user through the comparison of planned versus actual radio frequency measurement data.

The current contract, now in its last year of execution, provided a spectrum characterization and analysis software from the ground-up coding in micro-services that provided a Government-owned custom software that implements a hardware agnostic interface, all targeted to support the WGS-11 satellite while being able to support all prior WGS satellites. This software and hardware solution is integrated with all current Wideband Control interface subsystems and maintains current performance specifications.

The desired end-result of this forthcoming contract is to sustain this fielded version of WRMS, WRMS version release 3 (WRMS v3.x), and to provide enhancements based on feedback from the users as well as to continue addressing current and new software backlog items. Please see the attached draft Performance Work Statement for more information.

PLEASE REVIEW ATTACHMENT 7571TE-26CSS-1525482-CSS FOR FURTHER DETAILS

This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued.

Solicitation No. 7571TE-26CSS-1525482 has been issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for a ﬁrm-ﬁxed-price commercial services purchase order for Cisco SmartNet support services to maintain, support, and enhance the operational readiness of Cisco network devices for the Indian Health Service, California Area federal facilities

BACKGROUND: The Indian Health Service (IHS), an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), is responsible for delivering federal health services to members of federally recognized tribes. IHS operates a geographically dispersed network infrastructure supporting clinical and administrative systems across multiple locations in the California Area, including Arcata, Clovis, Davis, Escondido, Hemet, Redding, Sacramento, and Ukiah.

Reliable network operations are critical to ensuring uninterrupted healthcare delivery. Cisco network infrastructure forms the backbone of these operations.

PURPOSE: The purpose of this contract is to procure Cisco SmartNet support services to maintain, support, and enhance the operational readiness of Cisco network devices. SmartNet service shall:

• Provide 24x7x365 access to Cisco Technical Assistance Center (TAC)

• Enable rapid hardware replacement (2-hour, 4-hour, or next business day based on service level)

• Provide access to IOS/IOS-XE software updates, patches, and security ﬁxes

• Deliver proactive security alerts and vulnerability notiﬁcations

• Support lifecycle and asset management via Cisco Smart Net Total Care portal

SCOPE OF WORK: The Contractor shall provide Cisco SmartNet support coverage for twenty-seven (27) 

Cisco devices and associated licenses. Services shall include technical support, hardware replacement, software updates, and proactive monitoring. More details per device (including device serial numbers) can be found in Attachment 2 - SmartNet Speciﬁcations Listing excel spreadsheet.

PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The anticipated period of performance includes one (1) 12-month base period and two (2) 12-month option periods. The base period is September 30, 2026, through September 29, 2027. Each option period, if exercised, will continue for 12 months following the prior performance period.

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Services shall support equipment located at IHS California Area federal facilities including: Arcata, Clovis, Davis, Escondido, Hemet, Redding, Sacramento, and Ukiah.

Set-Aside: Indian Small Business Economic Enterprise (ISBEE) Set-Aside under the Buy Indian Act 

NAICS Code: 541519 - Other Computer Related Services.

Small Business Size Standard: $34 million average annual receipts

Product Service Code: DA10 - IT and Telecom - Business Application/Application Development Software as a Service.

Issue Date: September 8, 2026

Quotation Due Date: September 14, 2026, at 3:00 PM Eastern Time

Submit Quotations To: miguel.diaz@hhs.gov

Email Subject Line: 7571TE-26CSS-1525482 – Cisco SmartNet Services

This requirement is set aside for Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEE). Under the Buy Indian Act, oﬀers are solicited only from Indian Economic Enterprises that are also small business concerns under the applicable NAICS code. Oﬀers received from enterprises that are not both Indian Economic Enterprises and small business concerns will not be considered and will be rejected.

Oﬀerors shall submit a completed IHS Indian Economic Enterprise Representation Form with the quotation. The oﬀeror shall remain eligible as an Indian Economic Enterprise at the time of quotation, at the time of award, and throughout contract performance. If an oﬀeror proposes to use subcontractors or teaming partners, the quotation shall clearly identify the proposed subcontracting or teaming arrangement and show how the prime oﬀeror will comply with applicable Buy Indian Act subcontracting limitations.

ATTACHMENTS

- Attachment 1 - Performance Work Statement

- Attachment 2 - SmartNet Speciﬁcations Listing excel spreadsheet

INSTRUCTIONS TO RESPONDENTS 

Submission of Quotes: Quotations shall be submitted electronically to miguel.diaz@hhs.gov no later than September 14, 2026, at 3:00 PM Eastern Time. The email subject line should read: 7571TE-26CSS-1525482 – Cisco SmartNet Services.

The Government may consider a quotation received after the due date and time only if the Contracting Oﬃcer determines that doing so would not unduly delay the acquisition and would be in the Government interest. Oﬀerors are responsible for ensuring timely receipt.

Quotes shall include:

notices.title: Consolidated Product-Line Management, Sustainment, and Modernization (CPMSM)
notices.agency_path: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.AMC.ACC.ACC-CTRS.ACC-APG.W6QK ACC-APG-ORLANDO
notices.description_text:
1. Purpose

The purpose of this notice is to obtain information and industry comments in anticipation of a future competitive requirement for the Consolidated Product-Line Management, Sustainment, and Modernization (CPMSM) program, which will continue supporting the objectives of the Consolidated Product-Line Management Plus (CPM Plus) program, focusing on the requirements, development, execution, management, and synchronization of the Live Training Transformation (LT2) Product-Line (P/L).

 With 23 LT2 products fielded to over 200 sites globally, the LT2 P/L successfully employs technical and acquisition strategies that significantly reduce fielding time, minimize acquisition costs, enable total ownership cost reductions, and enhance training benefits afforded to the warfighter.

The incumbent contractor for the existing CPM Plus effort under contract number W900KK-20-D-0007 is General Dynamics Mission Systems, Inc., 12001 Research Parkway Ste 500, Orlando, FL 32826-3249.

2. Program Description

The planned CPMSM contract vehicle will encompass the continued management of the evolution of the LT2 P/L and provide total life cycle support to those programs that utilize the LT2 P/L. It will continue to meet the requirements for a consolidated streamlined approach that:

1) Protects and leverages the Army's LT2 P/L investment.

2) Continues the development and evolution of the LT2 products/systems, core assets, architectural frameworks, and the LT2 P/L Construct.

3) Continues to provide efficient, effective, and agile methods to deliver military training products.

Under the CPMSM program the Army will execute control of a system's life cycle within a System-of-Systems (SoS) environment to maximize the commonality, reuse and interoperability of the system, while maintaining integrity of the product lines from which it is based. CPMSM will continue to evolve the deliberate processes for managing the development, production, and sustainment of LT2 products. CPMSM will enable using organizations to maintain visibility and control of the configuration of those systems, and SoS integration for which they are responsible throughout the total system life cycle.

The anticipated nature and complexity of the LT2 P/L work tasks (ranging from P/L architectural development, system development, SoS management to P/L core asset variability, and configuration management) associated with CPMSM requires mature and established processes, and therefore at least a Level 3 Capability Maturity Model Integration (CMMI) company rating.

3. Request For Information

The Government is conducting market research with companies that are interested in this requirement and/or portions therein. Specifically, the Government requests that companies address their capabilities and relevant experience as we inform our contracting strategy for CPMSM. The Government would also like to solicit feedback from industry on the recommended contracting strategy for the CPMSM effort.

4. Company Profile

To assist the Government in determining if this can be set aside for small businesses, please provide the following administrative information:

• Company Name, CAGE Code, and UEI Number.

• Point of Contact (Name, Phone, Email).

• Business Size Standard and Socio-Economic Status (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB) under NAICS Code: 541512 for Computer Systems Design or 541511 for Custom Computer Programming).

All strategies should strive to protect and leverage the Army's LT2 P/L investment, while evolving core assets and the LT2 Construct tools and processes to ensure technology relevance across the P/L.

A web-based portal hosts a reference library and contains a multitude of information related to LT2 and CPM efforts. The library is located at https://lt2portal.mil. If you do not already have a LT2 Portal account then please go to the site and register for an account (click on register on top right hand side of the LT2 Portal home page, then fill in the information requested.

5. Submission Instructions

The Government is exploring a range of acquisition strategies and plans to utilize the information gained from this White Paper to help further shape the acquisition strategy. Responses should be limited to a three (3) page max white paper, not including cover page, cover letter, table of contents and any other documentation submitted in response to Past Performance. Any proprietary concepts of information should be clearly identified as such. Submitted data and information will not be returned. Any information submitted in response to this RFI Notice is strictly voluntary. This notice is for information and planning purposes. The Government will not pay or otherwise reimburse respondents for information submitted. Industry is encouraged to suggest alternative NAICS codes that may better align with the requirements.

Disclaimer: This notice does not constitute an invitation for bids or a request for proposal and is not a commitment by the U.S. Government to procure subject products or services nor will the Government reimburse any parties for costs associated with this request. The Government will use the information received to forge its acquisition strategy. Additionally, all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. No basis for a claim against the Government shall arise as a result from a response to this RFI.

All correspondence and questions regarding this notice shall be directed to the Contracting Office POC and Program Office POC listed below: 

POINT OF CONTACT INFORMATION: 

Contracts POC: Reuel Dunn: reuel.p.dunn.civ@army.mil, 520-714-5529 

Program POC: Courtney Flugstad: courtney.s.flugstad.civ@army.mil, 520-692-4037

notices.title: NATO Business Opportunity: Contractor Support for Quantum Zero Beacon Project (QZBP)
notices.agency_path: COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY
notices.description_text:
Headquarters Supreme Allied Commander Transformation (HQ SACT) intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) for contractor support for the Quantum Zero Beacon Project (QZBP).

U.S. Prime Contractors and Subcontractors must 1) maintain a professionally active facility within the United States, 2) be approved for participation in NATO Competitive Procurement (NCP), 3) hold a Facility Security Clearance (FCL) at the level of SECRET or higher, and 4) be issued a Declaration of Eligibility (DOE) by the U.S. Government.

In addition, contractor personnel performing services under the contract must be citizens of a NATO nation, possess a security clearance at the level of SECRET or higher, and have appropriate professional training and experience in a related field.

The reference for the RFP is RFP-ACT-SACT-26-90 and all correspondence regarding the RFP should include this reference. 

DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT

HQ SACT is seeking contractor support to establish the conditions in which NATO can demonstrate and validate a practical pathway for NATO's transition to quantum-resilient communications by implementing a pilot deployment between two NATO enclaves – NATO HQ (Brussels) and SHAPE (Mons). HQ SACT is seeking contractor support capable of rapidly delivering, within one year, a limited-scale quantum-safe cryptography deployment within NATO operational networks. The project will provide operational evidence, technical lessons, and a transition roadmap to support broader NATO adoption of quantum-safe cryptography before 2030.

Additional support is expected to include, but is not limited to, program and stakeholder management; requirements and risk management; capability engineering, integration and testing; cryptographic and cyber-security expertise, including quantum threat vulnerability assessment post quantum cryptography expertise and implementation; security accreditation and operational validation; IT/CIS specialist support; performance, interoperability and migration assessments; and business management support. Contractor support will also cover the development of Quantum safe migration roadmaps, policy recommendations, lessons learned, and demonstration activities supporting NATO capability transition and wider exploitation.

QZBP is an integral part of NATO's quantum-related policy and roadmap activities, including NATO Quantum Strategy, supporting the Alliance's transition towards quantum-safe and crypto-agile capabilities. The project, limited to 12 months, will address short- and medium-term requirements through the operational experimentation and validation of mature Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) solutions, while generating the evidence, lessons learned and migration considerations required to inform NATO's longer-term transition to quantum-safe cryptography. In doing so, QZBP will contribute to reducing emerging cryptographic risks, validating operationally relevant approaches, and informing future NATO-wide capability development and implementation activities.

HQ SACT will apply a Sealed Bidding Procedure in accordance with the Procurement Policy for NATO Common Funding.

Place of performance: NATO HQ, Brussels (Belgium); SHAPE, Mons (Belgium); NCIA, The Hague (The Netherlands), Contractor facility (TBC).

BECOMING ELIGIBLE TO BID 

NCP requires that the U.S. Government issue a DOE on behalf of potential U.S. prime contractors and subcontractors interested in this contract. Before the U.S. Government can do so, however, the U.S. Government must approve the U.S. firm for participation in NCP. U.S. firms are approved for NCP on a facility-by-facility basis. 

The U.S. NCP application is a one-time application. The application requires supporting documentation in the form of 1) a company resume indicating contracts completed 2) an annual report or set of financial documents indicating compilation, review, or audit by an independent CPA.

U.S. firms can download a copy of the U.S. NCP application from the following website:

https://www.bis.gov/about-bis/bis-leadership-and-offices/SIES/business-opportunities-nato 

The Department of Commerce (DOC) is the U.S. Government agency that approves NCP applications. Please submit to the email address provided your application and supporting documentation (as attachments). If your firm is interested in a specific NCP project at this time, please also include the following in the text of your email:

- the title and/or solicitation number of the contract

- the name/phone/email of the company point of contact for the bid documents

After approval of your one-time NCP application, DOC will then know to follow up by issuing a DOE for the contract. DOC will transmit the DOE to the NATO contracting agency. 

IMPORTANT DATES

U.S. firms should request a DOE (and, for U.S. firms new to NCP, submit the one-time NCP application): 22 September 2026

HQ SACT issues RFP (planned): 28 September 2026

Bid closing (planned): 02 November 2026

Contract award (anticipated): 30 November 2026

This notice is for information and planning purposes only to assess industry capabilities and market potential. This RFI does not constitute an invitation for Bids, Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or solicitation. No solicitation document exists currently. This RFI constitutes no Government obligation to procure these items or issue a solicitation. PURPOSE

This is a Request for Information for the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) Defensive Cyber Systems Branch (HNCD). The purpose of this RFI is to conduct market research to identify commercial sources capable of providing a Next-Generation, Vendor-Agnostic Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) software solution.

The program office is seeking industry feedback on software solutions that meet or exceed the capabilities of enterprise orchestration platforms like Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR. The desired platform must avoid vendor ecosystem lock-in, support highly extensible modular open architectures, and be capable of deployment across enterprise cloud, garrison, and localized tactical edge environments on standard commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) computing baselines (referred to as the V+ platform architecture).

The government intends to evaluate solutions that offer robust, decentralized orchestration, a vast open-integration marketplace, native threat intelligence lifecycle management, and advanced Machine Learning (ML)-assisted analyst workflows.

notices.title: DA10--DB Protect Software and Maintenance Bridge  (VA-26-00089068)(New Work)
notices.agency_path: VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.TECHNOLOGY ACQUISITION CENTER NJ (36C10B)
notices.description_text: This requirement was for a firm-fixed price delivery order (DO) issued under National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Solution for Enterprise-Wide Procurement (SEWP) V Government wide Acquisition Contract (GWAC) contract NNG15SD20B with Cynergy Professional Systems LLC (Cynergy) to provide brand name TrustWave Holdings Inc. (TrustWave) DbProtect term software licenses with maintenance and technical support. Cynergy is a Small Business Administration Certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) that is an authorized reseller for brand name TrustWave DbProtect term software licenses with maintenance and technical support. TrustWave DbProtect licensing and support are proprietary and can only be procured directly from an authorized TrustWave provider. Because the database security environment relies on TrustWave s unique architecture, integrations, and maintenance protocols, any attempt to obtain licensing or support through an alternate source would result in delays, incompatibility risks, and unacceptable gaps in security coverage. Cynergy is the current provider and will ensure uninterrupted protection of mission critical systems. Without the required TrustWave DbProtect licensing, the VA would be unable to perform essential database vulnerability scans, leaving critical systems unmonitored. This inability to assess and identify security risks would place the VA s data and infrastructure under undue and unacceptable risk. No other brand name database vulnerability scanning platform is interoperable with VA s existing TrustWave DbProtect infrastructure, database structures, and software application programming interfaces due to the proprietary constraints of the TrustWave infrastructure currently implemented within VA. Specifically, due to the proprietary constraints within the software source code, any other Original Equipment Manufacturer s (OEM) solution would not be able to communicate with the VA s existing TrustWave software licenses to provide the necessary database scanning and database vulnerability data collection, as well as critical updates, patches, updates to TrustWave DbProtect's Shatter Knowledge database, and bug fixes needed to ensure the infrastructure continues to function as intended.
