notices.title: Operations, Research, and Broad Innovative Technology Services (ORBIT)   Request for Information (RFI) and Sources Sought Notice (SSN)
notices.agency_path: NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION.NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION.NASA JOHNSON SPACE CENTER
notices.description_text:
THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. NO PROPOSALS ARE TO BE SUBMITTED IN RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE.

The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center (JSC) Flight Operations Directorate (FOD) is hereby solicitating information from potential sources for the Operations, Research, and Broad Innovative Technology Services (ORBIT) solicitation. NASA JSC is issuing this RFI/SSN as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in, and the resources to support this requirement. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the type and method of procurement. A draft Statement of Work (dSOW) is in the attachment section for information and planning purposes and to allow industry the opportunity to verify reasonableness and feasibility of the requirement, as well as promote competition.

NASA JSC is seeking capability statements from all interested parties, including all socioeconomic categories of Small Businesses (SB) and Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU)/Minority Institutions (MI) for the purposes of determining the appropriate level of competition and/or small business subcontracting goals for ORBIT. Vendors are encouraged to demonstrate capabilities as a prime, subcontractor and/or teaming partner. The Government reserves the right to consider a Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), HUBZone, Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, and Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) business set-aside based on responses received. 

Respondents are requested to provide informed input on realistic and appropriate SB subcontracting and/or participation goals for the specific requirement. This type of feedback supports NASA's market research and helps ensure the acquisition strategy is aligned with actual industry capability. Industry feedback is requested for:

1. SB Subcontracting goals;

2. Barriers that may limit SB participation, such as certifications, unique technical requirements, security needs, specialized tools, or high-risk performance areas and/or

3. Strategies to increase SB participation, including:

• Breaking requirements into smaller components

• Identifying areas appropriate for subcontracting

• Considering teaming or mentor protégé approaches

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541512, Computer Systems Design Services, and the corresponding small business size standard is $34 million, calculated in accordance with 13 CFR 121.104.

ORBIT Description:

The proposed ORBIT contract will provide mission engineering, spaceflight-enabling, mission support, and advanced technology services to NASA's Flight Operations Directorate (FOD) at Johnson Space Center (JSC) and its mission partners. It is anticipated that the ORBIT will be a multiple-award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract vehicle with Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) task orders. 

This acquisition will establish a follow-on contract vehicle to succeed the Mission Enabling Support Contract MESC-IDIQ contracts, encompassing the legacy and a subset of those requirements including partial scope of MESC-B, which are scheduled to expire on September 30, 2027. The follow- on contract restructures the acquisition strategy to better align functionally related capability areas as part of a single procurement , reduces the contract administration burden on the Government, improves small business participation and competition at the task order level, and provides a more efficient and flexible contracting mechanism for the delivery of the following Functional Area Requirements identified in the dSOW:

• Functional Area 1 - Mission and Systems Engineering Support

• Functional Area 2 - Technical Evaluation, Analysis, and Independent Assessment

• Functional Area 3 Specialized IT and Operations

• Functional Area 4 - Advanced Mission R&D

No solicitation exists; therefore, do not request a copy of the solicitation. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on SAM.gov. Interested firms are responsible for monitoring this website for the release of any solicitation or synopsis.

Interested firms having the required capabilities necessary to meet the above requirement described herein should submit a capability statement of no more than 10 pages indicating the ability to perform all aspects of the effort.

Capability Statement:

Interested firms having the required capabilities necessary to meet the above requirement should indicate the ability to perform all aspects of the effort, and include the following information:

1. Technical - Describe your company's overall skills, experience, and capabilities to perform the work of the ORBIT dSOW. Please identify specific dSOW sections where your company could provide the stated capability by way of Attachment 1 - Vendor Capability Matrix at the end of this announcement. If subcontracting or if a joint venture is anticipated, organizations should address the anticipated administrative and management structure of such arrangements (if this information is known at this time). Also address what elements of work would be performed by the prime or joint venture partners and which elements would be performed by subcontractors.

2. General –

a. What additional documents would you like to see on the ORBIT contract website or included in the Technical Library?

b. What barriers or obstacles do you foresee to potentially bidding on this contract? Can you identify any Government acquisition approaches that would increase the competitiveness of this procurement?

What innovations might you propose in the performance of this contract or contract structure? 

c. What innovations might you propose in the performance of this contract or contract structure?

3. Company-Specific Information - Responses must include the following:

a. Company's name, address, and a point of contact (name, e-mail address, and address)

b. Unique Entity Identifier number and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code

c. Number of years in business 

d. Size of business

i. Average annual revenue for past three years

ii. Number of employees

iii. Whether the firm is a Large, SB, Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), 

HUBZone, WOSB, Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB), SDVOSB, 

HBCU/MI, and/or 8a

e. Ownership, affiliate information (as applicable) including parent company and joint venture partners

f. If you plan to propose as a prime or as a subcontractor;

g. A list of contracts covering the past three years with emphasis on work performed for the United States Federal Government. Please provide contract numbers, if your firm was a prime or subcontractor, contract type, dollar value of each procurement, and customer point of contact (address, phone, and email). If work was performed as a subcontractor, please indicate percentage of work/subcontract dollar value. If the contract(s) were IDIQ, please indicate the number of task orders awarded and the total dollar value of those task orders.

h. Company's specific capabilities that are relevant to the requirements contemplated above. It is not sufficient to provide general brochures or generic information. 

This RFI/SSN is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. Respondents deemed fully qualified will be considered in any resultant solicitation for the requirement.

All responses must be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Officer at jsc-orbit-procurement@mail.nasa.gov no later than 5:00 PM CENTRAL DAYLIGHT TIME on October 05, 2026. Please reference "ORBIT Sources Sought" in the subject line of any response.

NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at : https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurement-Ombuds-Comp-Advocate-Listing.pdf

If a solicitation is released, then it and any additional documents will be available on Sam.gov. It is the offeror's responsibility to monitor this website for the release of the solicitation and amendments (if any). Potential offerors will be responsible for downloading their own copy of the solicitation and amendments, if any.

NASA intends to publicize a listing of respondents to facilitate teaming arrangements. Should your firm desire not to be included in this listing, clearly indicate this desire in your response.

notices.title: NCI Oncology Clinical Trial System, Management and Support
notices.agency_path: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH.NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH OLAO
notices.description_text:
Type of Notice:

This is a Small Businesses Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to determine (1) the availability and capability of qualified small business sources; (2) whether they are small businesses; HUBZone small businesses; service disabled veteran-owned small businesses; 8(a) small businesses; women-owned small businesses; or small disadvantaged businesses; and (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition. Your response to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. 

The NAICS code for this acquisition is 541512 – Computer Systems Design Services. The small business size standard is $34M.

Background:

The Cancer Therapy Evaluation Program (CTEP), National Cancer Institute (NCI), sponsors and coordinates a broad portfolio of clinical trials evaluating cancer treatments, ranging from early-phase studies to large-scale multi-site trials conducted through national research networks. CTEP relies on a suite of integrated enterprise applications to support protocol and study management, study activation, investigational agent/drug management, safety reporting, regulatory workflows, and data sharing and reporting across a large and diverse community of investigators, sites, and research networks.

CTEP's Enterprise System (CTEP-ESYS) is NCI's enterprise system environment for supporting the conduct, oversight, and evaluation of NCI-sponsored oncology clinical trials. It provides integrated applications, data repositories, interfaces, and services that support protocol development, study administration, regulatory oversight, user and site credentialing, investigational agent management, safety reporting, data exchange, and operational decision-making across the clinical trials enterprise.

Purpose and Objectives:

The goal of this acquisition is to identify qualified small business sources capable of providing enterprise-level informatics, application development, modernization, and operational support for CTEP-ESYS environment. The requirement supports complex biomedical, clinical research, healthcare, regulatory, and clinical trial operations, and may include, but is not limited to:

 Enterprise application operations, maintenance, and enhancement for large-scale, mission-critical enterprise applications and integrated application suites;

 Custom application development, re-engineering, modernization, and migration, including cloud-based or cloud-first modernization, while maintaining continuity of operations;

 Clinical trial and biomedical informatics support, including systems for protocol/study management, study activation, trial oversight, investigational agent/drug management, safety reporting, regulatory workflows, and clinical research data management;

 System integration, interoperability, and data exchange across Government and partner environments, including APIs, interfaces, data pipelines, reporting workflows, and data quality controls;

 Data management, reporting, analytics, automation, and AI/ML capabilities, including AI-assisted data extraction, classification, summarization, workflow automation, and decision-support tools where outputs support human review rather than replace Government or clinical decision-making;

 AI-assisted workflow support and governance, including data readiness assessment, model/tool evaluation, validation, monitoring, documentation, and governance of AI/ML-related activities

 Security, privacy, and compliance support for Federal information systems, including FISMA/NIST-based controls, identity and access management, vulnerability management, ATO support, audit logging, cloud security, backup/disaster recovery, and continuous monitoring; and

 User support, stakeholder coordination, and program management, including help desk support, stakeholder coordination, deliverables management, staffing, performance tracking, and surge support

These systems support mission-critical, uninterrupted clinical trial operations across multiple trial phases, research networks, participating sites, and investigators, and require modernization of legacy components without disruption to active operations.

CTEP-Specific Technical Considerations:

Respondents should also be prepared to address their ability to support:

 A suite of integrated custom applications rather than a single standalone system

 Mission-critical operations, maintenance, enhancement, modernization, and integration support

 Clinical trial workflows involving protocol/study management, study activation, trial oversight, investigational agent management, safety reporting, regulatory support, data sharing, and reporting

 Modernization of legacy components while maintaining uninterrupted support for active clinical trial operations

 Cloud modernization, application migration, DevSecOps, automated testing, release management, and production support

 Integration with multiple internal and external systems and partners

 AI-assisted or advanced analytical capabilities within existing enterprise workflows, such as protocol information extraction, workflow automation, reporting support, and decision-support functions

 Controlled evaluation and implementation of AI/ML or automation use cases with appropriate validation, documentation, security, data quality, traceability, and human oversight

 Enterprise IT operations, maintenance, and production support for custom application environments, including incident management, change management, release management, and service-level tracking

 Agile software development, systems analysis, requirements management, testing, configuration management, and documentation for custom application portfolios

 Database administration, data engineering, data repositories, reporting, dashboards, and business intelligence support

 API development, interface management, data exchange, and integration with internal Government systems and external partner systems

 Section 508, usability, and user experience considerations for systems used by Government, contractor, investigator, and research site users.

Note: Please only respond to this notice if you are capable of addressing the full range of capability areas described above.

Project Requirements:

A copy of the draft Statement of Work (SOW) pertaining to this requirement, which is subject to revision, is attached to this notice.

Anticipated Period of Performance:

The anticipated period of performance, inclusive of options, for this proposed acquisition is July 1, 2027 – June 30, 2032. The Government anticipates making a single award, which may be issued as a contract or task order depending on the final acquisition strategy.

Capability Statement/Information Sought:

Small businesses possessing experience and demonstrated capability to accomplish the requirements described above are requested to submit a capability statement addressing the following:

 Capability and Experience – Describe your experience supporting enterprise systems, informatics, or application support systems for biomedical research, clinical trials, healthcare, regulatory, or scientific programs.

 Clinical Trial / Biomedical Informatics Experience – Describe your experience supporting systems involving protocol/study management, safety reporting, regulatory workflows, investigational agent/drug management, or clinical research data management.

 Application Development and Modernization – Describe your experience maintaining, enhancing, modernizing, and migrating custom applications in a complex multi-system environment while maintaining production operations.

 Interoperability and Data Exchange – Describe your experience integrating systems across multiple organizations, including APIs, data exchange, reporting, dashboards, data pipelines, and data quality controls.

 Advanced Analytics, Automation, and AI/ML – Describe your experience developing, integrating, or supporting advanced analytics, automation, or AI-assisted tools in Federal, biomedical, healthcare, clinical research, or regulated environments.

 AI Use Case Identification and Governance – Describe how you would identify, evaluate, validate, monitor, document, and govern AI-assisted capabilities used to support operational or decision-support workflows.

 Security and Compliance – Describe your experience supporting Federal security requirements, including FISMA/NIST-based controls, ATO support, vulnerability remediation, identity/access management, audit logging, cloud security, and systems handling sensitive Government or research data.

 Small Business Capability – Identify your business size and socioeconomic status under the anticipated NAICS code, and indicate whether your company could perform as a prime contractor or subcontractor.

 Commercial vs. Non-Commercial Availability – Identify whether commercial products, platforms, or services could meet all or a substantial portion of the requirement. If so, describe what portion could be met commercially and what would require customization, integration, or custom development.

 Enterprise IT / Informatics Services Capability – Describe your experience providing enterprise IT services for large custom application environments, including application operations and maintenance, software development, cloud support, DevSecOps, database/data engineering, system integration, cybersecurity, help desk/user support, and production support.

 Contract Type – Identify whether any portion of this requirement could be accomplished under a firm-fixed-price contract. If a firm-fixed-price contract is not feasible, identify the proposed contract type.

 Contract Vehicles – Identify any existing contract vehicles (e.g., GSA Schedules, other Government Wide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs)) that industry recommends for fulfilling this requirement.

Information Submission Instructions:

Information furnished must not exceed 12 pages (12-point font minimum), including all attachments, resumes, charts, etc., and should include an outline of previous or similar projects performed covering each requirement above. All responses must include the business concern's name, point of contact, address, and UEI number.

All capability statements sent in response to this Small Business Sources Sought notice must be sent electronically via email to Rosa Lopez, Contracting Officer at Rosa.Lopez@nih.gov in either MS Word or Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF) by September 17, 2026, 3:00PM ET. All responses must be received by the specified due date and time in order to be considered. Capability statements received after that date and time will not be considered.

Disclaimer and Important Notes:

This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization's qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. After a review of the responses received, a pre-solicitation synopsis and solicitation may be published on SAM.gov. However, responses to this notice will not be considered adequate responses to a solicitation.

Confidentiality:

No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response. The Government reserves the right to use any non-proprietary technical information in any resultant solicitation(s).

notices.title: Notice of Intent to Sole-Source: Globus High Assurance Subscription Renewal
notices.agency_path: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH.NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH OLAO
notices.description_text:
GENERAL

This notice is issued in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 12.201-1(c)(2), advertising the Government's intent to issue an award on a sole source basis under the authority established in RFO 12.102(a). The National Institutes of Health, Specialized Scientific Information Technology (SSIT) Division anticipates issuing a single Purchase Order (PO) to the following entity:

The University of Chicago

401 N. Michigan Avenue, Suite 900

Chicago, IL 60611

BACKGROUND

The intramural NIH campus utilizes Globus function as a service (FaaS) within the High-Performance Computation Biowulf Cluster as a centralized service for the NIH scientific community. Many NICHD scientists in the intramural NICHD community routinely transfer data to and from Helix/Biowulf and other major computational centers on campus, and it is vital for them to have appropriate, secure, and user-friendly tools such as Globus.

Globus at the University of Chicago is proprietary software and the only commercially available product that can properly maintain all the essential functionalities required in support of the intramural scientists need to transfer data to and from Helix/Biowulf. Globus utilizes a secure endoint to endpoint transfer system specifically developed for transferring high-performance research data - allowing the NICHD to transfer data exceeding several terabytes in size. Globus maintains transfer status in the event of network outages, minimizing negative impacts to transfer operations and research timelines. 

There is no other compatible software that can properly and adequately support the Government with this need. Market research indicates that Globus is the proprietary vendor and therefore, is a sole source.

RESPONSES

There will not be a solicitation or competitive Request for Quotation (RFQ) issued as a result of this announcement. Any responses or inquiries to this notice must demonstrate clear and convincing evidence that competition will be advantageous to the Government. 

Notwithstanding the stated intent, if other organizations believe they can fully meet the Government's requirement, they must submit written documentation of their capabilities. The capabilities statement must contain sufficient documentation to establish a bona fide capability to fulfill the requirement and must be received by the response date listed in this posting. A general statement which merely states the entity is capable will not be sufficient. A determination not to compete with this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. 

NIH will not be responsible for any costs incurred by interested parties in responding to this notice. Acknowledgement of receipt of responses will not be made, nor will respondents be notified of the evaluation of the information received. Interested parties may respond and provide a capability statement no later than the date specified in this notice. Emails must reference the announcement number in the subject line. This is not an RFQ, and this announcement does not commit the Government to award a contract.

notices.title: Sources Sought: Social Media Monitoring
notices.agency_path: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH.NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH OLAO
notices.description_text:
GENERAL

This is a Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified sources to perform a potential requirement.

This notice is issued to help determine the availability of qualified companies technically capable of meeting the Government requirement, to determine the method of acquisition. It is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. 

BACKGROUND

The Division of Population Health Research (DiPHR) within the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development, requires automated collection and management of large-scale public social media data related to food, nutrition, eating behaviors, hunger, and sentiment from platforms such as Instagram, Facebook, and X (Twitter). Access to these services will accelerate research productivity and generate preliminary data for future external funding opportunities.

SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS

The DiPHR has utilized Apify in the past, and is seeking information on this and other comparable solutions available commercially. The solution must provide scalable data acquisition capabilities that enable efficient collection of millions of text, image, and video records needed for artificial intelligence (AI), Large Language Models (LLMs), computer vision, and machine learning analyses. Data acquisition must be timely, reproducible, and conducted on a large-scale. Additionally, the solution must:

 Collect public social media data from multiple platforms, including Instagram, Facebook, and X (Twitter), to support research on food, nutrition, eating behaviors, hunger, and public sentiment.

 Feature automated, scalable data extraction capable of collecting millions of text, image, video, engagement, and metadata records to meet study data collection needs.

 Facilitate structured data export and storage capabilities (e.g., JSON, CSV) to support efficient data management, reproducibility, and integration with research workflows.

 Possess scheduling and automation features that enable continuous or periodic data collection to support longitudinal monitoring and trend analyses.

 Incorporate data quality controls, including filtering, deduplication, and validation features, to improve data accuracy and reliability. 

 Allow for API access and compatibility with artificial intelligence (AI), natural language processing (NLP), computer vision, machine learning, and Large Language Model (LLM) workflows to support advanced analyses.

 Maintain secure cloud-based infrastructure and data management capabilities to support compliant and efficient research operations.

REQUESTED INFORMATION

The Government requests feedback from interested parties regarding potential sources for solutions meeting the requirements in this notice. Interested parties submitting a response are asked to include the following information:

 Organization name, including any "DBA" if applicable.

 Universal Entity Identifier (UEI)

 Business size and socioeconomic category

 Capabilities statement for the organization

 Technical capabilities of the solution

 A rough order of magnitude (ROM) or a commercial price list which can be utilized to determine estimated pricing for 12-months of services.

notices.title: Patient Flow and Queue Management System - Crownpoint Healthcare Facility
notices.agency_path: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF.INDIAN HEALTH SERVICE.NAVAJO AREA INDIAN HEALTH SVC
notices.description_text:
The Indian Health Service (IHS), Navajo Area, Crownpoint Healthcare Facility, has a requirement for a commercially available Patient Flow and Queue Management System, ACF Technologies Q-Flow Brand Name or Equal, for the Crownpoint Healthcare Facility Pharmacy Department.

The requirement includes software and licensing, hardware, implementation, installation, system and workflow configuration, testing, training, warranty, maintenance, and technical support necessary to provide a fully operational patient flow and queue management solution. The system will support patient check-in, virtual queuing, appointment management, queue monitoring, patient notifications, digital signage, reporting, administrative dashboards, audit logging, role-based access, and related patient flow management functions.

The proposed solution shall operate as a standalone application within the Crownpoint Healthcare Facility network and shall comply with the operational, performance, cybersecurity, and other requirements identified in the solicitation and Statement of Work (SOW).

The anticipated period of performance consists of a 12-month base period and four (4) one-year option periods.

This acquisition is anticipated to be issued as a Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS 541519 – Other Computer Related Services. Quoters proposing an equal product shall demonstrate that the proposed solution meets the salient characteristics identified in the solicitation.

Interested parties shall review the complete solicitation and all attachments for the Government's requirements, quotation submission instructions, and evaluation criteria.

This notice constitutes the solicitation. Quotations shall be submitted in accordance with the instructions contained in the attached RFQ.

notices.description_text:
This is not a solicitation, and quotes are not being accepted at this time.

The 355th Contracting Squadron intends to issue a sole-source contract action for procurement of the following items:

 CLIN 0001 - Preventative Maintenance and Inspection

 CLIN 1001 - Preventative Maintenance and Inspection

 CLIN 2001 - Preventative Maintenance and Inspection

 CLIN 3001 - Preventative Maintenance and Inspection

 CLIN 4001 - Preventative Maintenance and Inspection

The Government intends to issue a sole source award for Preventative Maintenance and Inspection (PMI) services for the Monaco D‑21 Fire Alarm Reporting System currently installed across Davis‑Monthan AFB. This requirement is a follow‑on procurement to Contract FA487722F0066 for a five year contract (Base Year plus Four Option Years). The existing system architecture remains fully proprietary to Monaco Enterprises Incorporated (MEI), and MEI retains exclusive ownership of all software, firmware, communication protocols, and integration pathways associated with the D‑21 system.

All interested parties must respond no later than 18 September 2026 at 1200 PM ET to Kody McPherson at kody.mcpherson.1@us.af.mil and Contracting Officer Jerry Sauder at jerry.sauder.1@us.af.mil. Responses received will be reviewed in detail; however, a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely at the discretion of the Government. Information received will be evaluated exclusively to determine whether a competitive procurement is appropriate.

The 355th Contracting Office will not reimburse parties for any costs associated with submitting capability information.

Interested vendors are encouraged to review the Intent to Sole Source Letter for additional details and RFO references.

notices.title: Notice of Intent for NIH/NCATS (RDCRN) Pantheon Licenses and Support Renewal
notices.agency_path: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF.OFFICE OF THE ASSISTANT SECRETARY FOR ADMINISTRATION (ASA)
notices.description_text:
THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT, NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. A REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) WILL NOT BE ISSUED AND QUOTES WILL NOT BE REQUESTED.

The National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS) Rare Diseases Clinical Research Network (RDCRN) intends to award a firm fixed price sole source contract under the authority of FAR 12.102(a), only one source being available to meet the Government's needs, to:

Carahsoft Technology Corp

11493 Sunset Hills Road

Suite 100

Reston, VA 20190

NCATS hereby submits a notice of intent to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order for the renewal of the existing Pantheon Platform Licenses and Support which includes associated maintenance, upgrades, and technical support, for a twelve (12) month period of performance commencing within thirty (30) days of award.

Pantheon is required as the specified brand name because the RDCRN consortia websites and the network site (www.rarediseasenetwork.org) were built on and are currently hosted within the Pantheon platform, and the renewal continues an established production environment whose configuration, versioning history, automated backups, and Drupal upgrade cadence are natively integrated into Pantheon's proprietary infrastructure. This is not a new requirement. Although this contract is now expired, the requirement remains current and ongoing. Continued access to the platform is necessary to avoid interruption to established scientific and informatics workflows that support NCATS research. 

The platform's specific capabilities—Multidev on-demand development environments, Autopilot automated updates with visual regression testing, Custom Upstreams for template-based site creation, 24/7 technical support, and optional WordPress Multisite support available only on the Gold plan—are proprietary to Pantheon and cannot be replicated by an alternate vendor without migrating all consortia sites, rebuilding development and deployment workflows, and reconstructing the acquisition, analysis, and processing pipeline for scientific data, including data tied to research initiated prior to 1/20/2026. Any substitution would introduce operational downtime, risk to data integrity and visual consistency, and significant re-engineering cost, making Pantheon the only product that meets the Government's need for continuity of the existing hosting system.

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541519 Other Related Computer Services business size $34M.

The period of performance will be for one (1) 12-month base period from date of award to September 10, 2026 – July 14, 2027.

This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation document exists for the requirement. This hereby constitutes a synopsis of the requirement.

CLOSING STATEMENT

The determination not to compete this proposed contract action is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not be responsible for any costs incurred by responding to this notice. This is NOT a request for quotes or proposals.

Questions or comments to this Notice of Intent should be directed to the Primary Point of Contact

Leah L. Hinson via e-mail only Leah.Hinson@hhs.gov (no phone calls/voice mail). Messages regarding questions will not be accepted and will not receive a response). Please indicate in the subject of your email: Notice of Intent Question Submission – PCA-NCATS–08266 Pantheon Licenses and Support Renewal.

Contracting Office Address:

Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS) 

Office of Acquisitions (OA) | Assistant Secretary for Financial Resources (ASFR)

U.S. Department of Health and Human Services 

Primary Point of Contact:

Leah L. Hinson- Leah.Hinson@hhs.gov

notices.description_text:
Amendment 02: The purpose of this amendment is to post the Question & Answer document that was inadvertently not included yesterday. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged.

__________________

 

Amendment 01: The purpose of this amendment is to provide anonymized questions and answers for the requirement. The requirements document is revised to reflect answers to questions, as is the solicitation document itself, as attached. Changes are tracked in the revised documents. The solicitation response deadline is revised to September 4, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged. 

___________________

(I) This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in part 12 - Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued.

(II) The solicitation number is 1333ND26QNB670452 and this solicitation is a Request for Quotation (RFQ). This acquisition is being solicited as total small business set aside.

(III) The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 dated March 13, 2026, and the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) as updated through August 29, 2026, supplemented by Department of Commerce Acquisition Policy. 

(IV) The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 541519 – IT Value Added Resellers with a small business size standard of 150 employees.

(V) All quoters shall provide a firm fixed price quotation for the following line item(s):

Contract Line Item Number (CLIN)

TOTAL

Brand Name OR EQUAL Data Processing Server / GPU

Workstation for in accordance with the attached NIST

Requirements Document.

TOTAL:

(VI) The requirements for the line items to be acquired above are in the attached Requirements Document.

(VII) Date(s) and place(s) of delivery and acceptance and FOB point are required in accordance with the attached Requirements Document.

(VIII) Quoters/Contractors must possess an ACTIVE registration in the System for Award Management system, www.SAM.gov, when submitting a quotation and shall continue to be registered until time of award, during performance, and through final payment of any contract resulting from this solicitation. The Contracting Officer shall confirm that quoters have an "active" registration at the www.sam.gov website upon receipt of the quotation. If the SAM.gov registration is not active, the quotation will not be considered for award. Note that "ID Assigned" is not "Active." 

(IX) The provision at FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors—Commercial Products and Commercial Services (DEVIATION Jan 2026), applies to this acquisition. See Addendum to FAR 52.212-1 below.

Addendum to FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors – Commercial Products and Commercial Services (DEVIATION Jan 2026):

DUE DATE FOR QUOTATIONS

Quoters shall submit their electronic quotations, via email, so that NIST receives them not later than 11:00 AM Eastern Time on September 2, 2026. E-mail quotations shall be submitted directly to the Contract Specialist at laure.roller@nist.gov.

Please reference the RFQ number in the subject line of all email communications. Quotations which do not reference the RFQ number in the subject line may not be considered. Quotations shall not be deemed received by the Government until the quotation is received in the e-mail inbox set forth above.

INQUIRIES:

Quoters must submit all questions concerning this solicitation in writing to both the Contract Specialist Ms. Lauren Roller at lauren.roller@nist.gov. Questions should be received no later than August 28, 2026. All responses to timely submitted questions will be made in writing, without identification of the questioner, and will be included in an amendment to the solicitation. Even if provided in other form, only the responses included in the amendment to the solicitation will be deemed as the Government's formal response and govern performance of the contract.

Quotation Preparation Instructions: 

All quotations shall conform to solicitation provisions/clauses and be prepared in accordance with this section. The quotation shall be clearly and concisely written as well as be neat and logically assembled. All pages of the quotation shall be appropriately numbered.

The Quoter's quotation shall be clearly divided into the following distinct volumes:

Volume I – Technical Quotation

Volume II – Price Quotation

Volume III- Terms and Conditions

Volume I - Technical Quotation:

The Quoter shall submit one (1) copy of their technical quotation, electronically, via E-mail to the Contract Specialist identified above. The technical quotation shall address the following:

Technical Capability:

 Technical description and/or product literature. Quoters shall include the manufacturer, make and model of the product, manufacturer sales literature, or other product literature that CLEARLY DOCUMENTS that the quoted products meet or exceed all BRAND NAME OR EQUAL specifications outlined in the Requirements Document. The quoter is responsible for ensuring the submitted documentation clearly addresses all specifications and requirements.

 

 Country of origin of all manufactured end products quoted

 

 Confirmation of the quoter's ability to meet the required delivery terms.

 

 Confirmation of the quoter's ability to meet warranty requirements.

Volume II - Price Quotation:

The quoter shall submit one (1) copy of their entire quotation, electronically, via E-mail to the Contract Specialist identified above. The price quotation shall address, at minimum, the following information.

 The solicitation number

 

 The name, phone number, and email address of the quoter's/contractor's point of contact;

 

 Unique Entity Identifier # for quoter's/contractor's active SAM.Gov registration.

 

 A firm fixed price for each required line item, including a unit price and total amount where applicable, and the aggregate quoted firm fixed price for the requirement.

 

 Shipping and Delivery costs must be included in the quotation either as a separate line item or contained in the total price of the quote. The quotation shall include a total firm fixed price for the requirement that includes all shipping/delivery costs

 

 Any applicable discount terms.

Volume III – Terms and Conditions:

The quoter shall review the provision and clauses attachment and complete any required information as record via a separate volume response to this solicitation. 

Note: System updates may lag policy updates. The System for Award Management (SAM) may continue to require entities to complete representations based on provisions that are not included in this solicitation. Contracting officers will rely on representations from offers based on provisions in the solicitation. Entities are not required to, nor are they able to, update their entity registration to remove these representations in SAM.

Acceptance of Terms and Conditions:

If the contractor objects to any of the terms and conditions contained in this solicitation, the contractor shall state "The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award document with the exception, deletion, or addition of the following:" [Contractor shall list exception(s) and rationale for the exception(s)]. It is the sole responsibility of the contractor to identify in their quotation any exceptions to the terms and conditions of the solicitation. If the contractor does not include such a statement, the submission of a quotation in response to this solicitation will be regarded as the Contractor's acceptance of the Government's terms and conditions for inclusion into the resultant purchase order (PO). 

Note: This procurement is not being conducted under the GSA Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program or another Government-Wide Area Contract (GWAC). If a quoter submits a quotation based upon an FSS or GWAC contract, the Government will accept the proposed price. However, the terms and conditions stated herein will be included in any resultant purchase order, not the terms and conditions of the Quoter's FSS or GWAC contract, and the statement required above shall be included in the quotation. 

FAR 52.212-2 Evaluation- Commercial Products and Commercial Services (DEVIATION Jan 2026)

 Evaluation factors. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible Offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors will be used to evaluate offers:

The Government intends to award a single purchase order (PO) from this solicitation utilizing simplified acquisitions procedures in accordance with FAR part 12 of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul. The Government reserves the right not to award a PO or to make an award without discussions based solely upon initial quotes.

Basis for Award: 

Award will be made to the responsible quoter whose quotation, conforming to the solicitation, is the lowest priced, technically acceptable quote.

A quoter's failure to address any factor may be considered indicative of the quoter's lack of understanding of the Government's requirements and may result in the offer being determined unacceptable.

Evaluation Factors:

A quotation will be determined technically acceptable if it meets the following criteria:

 

(1) Technical Capability: The Quoter must indicate in its quotation the ability to provide all minimum brand name OR EQUAL requirements identified in the Requirements Document, inclusive of warranty requirements.

(2) Schedule: The Quoter must indicate in its quotation the ability to meet the delivery requirements within 30 days ARO. Additionally, delivery must be on a F.O.B Destination basis and inclusive of all delivery costs, including any potential tariffs.

 

(3) Price: The quoted price will be evaluated. The evaluation will determine whether the proposed prices are reasonable in relation to the solicitation requirements. Prices must be entirely compatible with the technical portion of the quotation.

(b) Options (if applicable). The Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total price for all options to the total price for the basic requirement. The Government may determine that an offer is unacceptable if the option prices are significantly unbalanced. The evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise the option(s).

 

(c) Notice of award. A written notice of award or acceptance of an offer furnished to the successful Offeror within the time for acceptance specified in the offer, shall result in a binding contract without further action by either party. Before the offer's specified expiration time, the Government may accept an offer (or part of an offer), whether or not there are negotiations after its receipt, unless a written notice of withdrawal is received before award.

 

(End of provision)

notices.agency_path: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.AIR FORCE MATERIEL COMMAND.AIR FORCE LIFE CYCLE MANAGEMENT CENTER.INTELLIGENCE, SURVEILLANCE, RECONNAISSANCE.FA8629 AFLCMC WISK SOF/PR
notices.description_text:
This Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS)/Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational purposes and market research only; it does not constitute a solicitation. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for any expenses associated with preparing/submitting information in response to this posting. The information provided may be used by the Government in developing its acquisition strategy, statement of work/statement of objectives, and/or performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained within their response as instructed later in this posting.

The United States (US) Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance & Special Operations Forces (ISR & SOF) Directorate, Special Warfare (SW) Program Office (AFLCMC/WISN) is conducting market research to identify possible sources capable of providing Wide Area Infrared Surveillance (WAIS) System.

REQUIREMENT

Key Performance Parameters (KPPs)

1. Performance & Detection Capabilities

• Passive Operation: Provide self-protection and situational awareness without emitting detectable signals.

• Detection & Tracking Capacity: Automatically detect and classify up to 100 simultaneous thermal signatures within 1 second.

• Detection Ranges: Capable of long-range acquisition across multiple target profiles:

• Commercial aircraft up to 93 miles (at 12,000 ft altitude).

• Group 2 Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) up to 10 miles.

• Personnel and ground vehicles up to 5 miles.

• Personnel detection minimum range is 500 meters.

• Tracking Accuracy & Reliability: Achieve a 90% overall detection probability. Target tracking accuracy must maintain ±3 degrees at 10 miles and ±5 degrees at 93 miles (evaluated at a 95% confidence level).

• Field of View (FOV): The entire system, comprised of multiple sensors, shall provide a minimum of 360° horizontal and 125° vertical hemispherical coverage.

• Individual sensors shall have a minimum FOV of 90 degrees.

• AI & Automation: Utilize advanced AI/ML-driven algorithms for automated target detection, classification (e.g., distinguishing small drones from commercial airliners), predictive analysis, and pattern recognition.

2. Integration & Interoperability

• C2 Integration: Incorporate an open-architecture design to integrate seamlessly with Command and Control (C2) systems, existing Tactical Grid infrastructure, and TACP mission software/hardware.

• Sensor Fusion: Capable of fusing multiple passive IR data streams (from within the IRIS-P system), and fusing with active radar and other external EO/IR sensors to deliver comprehensive, multi-domain situational awareness.

• Communication Standards: Utilize common tactical interface standards (e.g., MIL-STD-6016) to interface natively with broader electromagnetic spectrum awareness systems.

3. System Operations & Data Management

• Usability: Operable by a single user with minimal training. Features a user-friendly laptop workstation interface providing real-time data, tracking options, and automated alerts accessible within 3 seconds of a request.

• Operator Verification: Support robust "operator-in-the-loop" workflows to verify, refine, and override automated threat detections.

• Networking & Throughput: Process high-fidelity thermal imaging data at a minimum of 1 Gbps throughput on a hard-wired, closed network. Supports real-time data streaming, efficient data compression, and on-demand retrieval.

• Security & Storage: Implement role-based and security-clearance-based access control for stored data. Support Unencrypted, Type 3, and Type 1 communication pathways (Type-1 encryption specifically required for sensor data in transit).

• Data storage shall be scalable to accommodate increasing data volumes.

4. Physical Characteristics (SWaP) & Environmental Durability

• Deployability: Modular, low Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP) footprint. Deployable in rugged environments across mobile (dismounted, vehicle-mounted) and stationary (tripods, fixed towers) configurations. Minimize time and effort required to relocate stationary configuration.

• Environmental Ruggedization: Must meet MIL-STD-810G standards. Fully operational in extreme temperatures (-30°C to 55°C) and adverse weather conditions (rain, fog, snow).

Please see attachment for additional information regarding this requirement and instructions on responding to this Request for Information.

notices.description_text:
General Announcement

THIS NOTICE OF INTENT/SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATION PURPOSES ONLY.

Program Manager, Intelligence and Cyberspace Operations (PM ICO) within Portfolio Acquisition Executive – Marine Corps (PAE-MC) provides this sources sought and notice of intent to award on a sole-source basis in accordance with 10 United States Code (U.S.C.) §3204 (a)(1), as implemented by the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1(b) to Anduril Industries Inc., 1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa CA 92626-1548, CAGE: 85LD7, Unique Entity Identifier: KC3CH2MSK7Q3. The PMICO has a requirement for the procurement of fifteen (15) Maritime Targeting Cell (MTC) Shelter Systems, comprising (8) eight Operator Shelters and seven (7) Processing Shelters. These highly specialized, expeditionary, road-transportable, dual-shelter systems are required to support the urgent operational imperatives and timelines of the MTC program. These systems will provide a secure, self-contained, and ruggedized operating environment for conducting sensitive intelligence operations in contested and austere forward-deployed environments.

 2. Basis for Sole-Source Justification

Comprehensive market research was conducted across industry, including the evaluation of various vendor capability statements submitted in response to a previously posted Request for Information. Based on the responses received and technical analysis of market capabilities, the following was determined:

 Intended Source & Lack of Competition: Anduril Industries Inc. (1400 Anduril, Costa Mesa CA 92626-1548) is the only known source capable of satisfying the Government's urgent operational requirements without unacceptable technical risk, cost duplication, and schedule delay. Competition is lacking because no other vendor possesses a mature, field-tested production configuration that provides turnkey integration with the Government-specified MEP-1070 generator set while concurrently meeting all expeditionary physical footprint, modularity, road-transportability, and operational security parameters.

 Technical & Integrated Architecture: The proprietary baseline developed by Anduril Industries provides pre-engineered structural, environmental, and tactical power integration with the required MEP-1070 generator set. This turnkey architecture is critical to minimizing the logistical footprint, ensuring rapid deployment, and significantly reducing setup time in austere, forward-operating environments.

 Programmatic & Schedule Impact: Alternative vendor concepts reviewed during market research would require extensive re-engineering, power integration/distribution redesign, and developmental qualification, to include environmental and flight/road-transport certifications. Pursuing an alternative development effort would introduce programmatic delays, creating an unacceptable operational gap in meeting mission-critical fleet deployment timelines for the MTC program.

The Government anticipates award of a Firm-Fixed-Price delivery order, with a period of performance of approximately two (2) years. In tandem with executing this sole-source action and for all future opportunities, PM ICO will continue to conduct market research, monitor emerging industry capabilities, and actively pursue competitive acquisition strategies to the greatest extent practicable for future MTC program lifecycle and follow-on requirements.

 3. Capability Statement Submission Instructions

THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS.

However, all responsible sources may submit a technical capability statement, proposal, or quotation demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Government's operational and technical requirements. The Government will not be responsible for any cost incurred in responding to this notice; however, interested parties may identify their interest and capability to meet the operational and technical requirements and past performance data no later than 12:00pm local time, Quantico, VA on 17 September 2026. Submissions received within 15 calendar days of this publication will be considered by the Government. Information received will be evaluated solely for determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All submissions shall become Government property and will not be returned. The North American Industry Classification System code is 541512, Computer Systems Design Services. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 7F20, IT and Telecom – IT Management Tool/Products (Hardware and Perpetual License Software).

All responses to this notice shall be submitted to Mr. Jeffrey Newton at jeffrey.l.newton@usmc.mil and Ms. Brittney Moore at brittney.moore@usmc.mil. Please reference the notification identification number on all responses. Telephone calls will not be honored.

notices.title: Hardware and Software - 3 infiniband director switches renewal
notices.agency_path: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
notices.description_text:
Solicitation Number: 7571TE26Q00257

Notice Type: Notice of Intent to Sole Source

Title: Hardware and Software - 3 infiniband director switches renewal

Description:

The National Institute of Health (NIH) intends to award a sole source purchase order for Center of Information Technology (CIT), for Hardware and Software - 3 infiniband director switches renewal. The North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) is 541519.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company (HPE) is the only responsible source known to provide the services needed.

It is NIH's intent that the proposed action may be awarded on a sole source basis to Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company (HPE) under the authority of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 13 Simplified Acquisition Procedures.

Contractor Objectives and Tasks:

The purpose of this acquisition is:

To renew On Premise Limfinity License 1 x production and 2 non-production 30 x Concurrent User Licenses

Standard Maintenance and Support Plan

Includes:

Continued hardware maintenance and technical support for three (3) existing Mellanox 648-port InfiniBand director switches supporting the Biowulf high-performance computing environment.

Biowulf is the centralized NIH-wide high-performance computing resource supporting scientific computing across the NIH Intramural Research Program. The InfiniBand network infrastructure provides the high-speed connectivity necessary for Biowulf computing resources to communicate efficiently and support computationally intensive scientific research.

The three Mellanox 648-port InfiniBand director switches covered by this requirement are existing components of the Biowulf high-performance computing network. Continued manufacturer maintenance and technical support are required to maintain the operational availability and reliability of this critical network infrastructure.

The required support includes HPE Tech Care Basic with Defective Media Retention (wDMR), hardware technical support, onsite support, replacement parts, and Basic Service Level support.

This is not a solicitation, nor is a solicitation available. However, all interested organizations may submit their capability statements and qualifications which will be considered by NIH. Responses must be in writing and must be submitted electronically to Damian Hurge, Contract Specialist at Damian.Hurge@HHS.gov by 11:00 AM EST on, September 4, 2026. Proposals must include pricing information. No late responses will be accepted.

Disclaimer and Important Notes: This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization's qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted.

Confidentiality: No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response. The Government reserves the right to use any non-proprietary technical information.

notices.description_text:
Notice of Intent to Sole Source – ANARK Software Licenses, Maintenance, and Support

****Extended until 9/15/2026 12pm EST 

The Government intends to solicit and award, on a sole source basis, a Firm-Fixed-Price contract to Anark Corporation, 4775 Walnut Street, Suite 200, Boulder, CO 80301, for ANARK software licenses, maintenance, and support services in support of the Commander, Fleet Readiness Centers (COMFRC), Digital Group, Aviation Product Lifecycle Management (AvPLM) program. This requirement includes software maintenance and engineering support for Anark Core Server (ACS) and Anark Core Workstation (ACW) applications used in the AvPLM environment, as well as support for generating 3D Portable Document Format (PDF) files from Computer Aided Design (CAD) models and associated data files. The requirement also includes an option for professional service hours to support AvPLM integration activities related to ANARK tools and enhanced support services for configuring and extending Anark Publish within the AvPLM environment. Anark Corporation is the only known Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) capable of providing this proprietary software and associated support, and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Award is expected NLT 15 September 2026.

THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement for consideration by the agency. Capability statements shall be limited to five (5) pages, 8.5 x 11 inches, in Times New Roman font no smaller than 10-point and must be submitted in Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF format. Responses are due no later than 5:00 PM EST, Thursday, 3 September 2026. No classified information shall be submitted. No phone calls will be accepted. All responsible sources must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database at the following website: https://www.sam.gov/portal/public/SAM/.    ****Extended until 9/15/2026 12pm EST 

Questions and capability statements shall be submitted via email to melissa.m.walker43.civ@us.navy.mil or alternate point of contact meghan.e.huett.civ@us.navy.mil If a responding vendor is not the OEM, the response must include proof of authorized reseller status from the OEM. The applicable NAICS code is 541519 and the PSC is DA10. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not pay for any information received.

notices.agency_path: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.AMC.ACC.ACC-CTRS.ACC RI.W6QK ACC-RI
notices.description_text:
U.S. Army Contracting Command – Rock Island (ACC-RI), on behalf of the Capability Program Executive Enterprise Software & Services (CPE ES2), Fort Belvoir, VA, intends to award a new non-competitive, single-award Firm-Fixed-Price Labor Hours (FFP-LH) contract to Augur Consulting, Inc. (CAGE Code: 659X0, UEID: ZLJNJG6DRZJ5), located at 1400 Crystal Dr. Suite 800, Arlington, VA 22202.

The proposed contract will be awarded on a sole-source basis under the authority of Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul 6.103-1, "Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements". 

This procurement is to provide highly specialized Operations Research and Systems Analysis (ORSA), cost estimating, and financial management support services. The scope of services covers the full range of ORSA methodologies, including parametric cost modeling (utilizing ACEIT, COCOMO, and SEER-SEM), life-cycle cost estimating, schedule risk analysis, data science, and advanced analytics. These services are critical to support informed acquisition, programming, and resource prioritization decisions across the CPE ES2 portfolio.

THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS/QUOTES. However, all responsible sources who believe they can meet the full scope of this requirement may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. Information received will be evaluated solely for the purpose of market research. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based upon responses received as a result of this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

notices.title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source ACF Technologies for Patient Queuing System Kiosk
notices.agency_path: VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.RPO WEST (36C24W)
notices.description_text:
Easy-to-use patient self-service kiosk, visual and audio mechanisms for patient notification, ease of use for laboratory personnel, provide reports for quality assurance purposes.

3.1. Patient Queuing System 3.1.1. System is capable of patient self-check-in with option to utilize existing Veteran Health Identification Card (VHIC)

3.1.2. System is capable of generating a ticket with sequentially numbered (alphanumeric) ticket. 3.1.2.1. System ticketing capability of SMS message to mobile device is a plus but not required.

3.1.3. System is capable of separating patients into multiple queues

3.1.4. Ability to move queued patients from one location, or queue, to another as needed

3.1.5. System capable of communications with multiple workstations simultaneously

3.1.6. System includes an audio system in patient waiting areas for audible patient notification

3.1.7. All required software, hardware, operating system, and database licenses must be included

3.1.8. System must be able to accommodate all users the Bakersfield Clinic as illustrated in

Attachment A – Schedule of Pricing, Tab 2. Site Requirements

3.1.9. Must be able to provide method for patient feedback to capture patient satisfaction

3.2. DA Section 508 requirements

3.2.1. Kiosks shall comply with ADA Section 508 requirements as applicable. Please see Attachment C – Section 508 Requirements.

3.3. Self-Check-in

3.3.1. System includes number of standup and desktop model kiosks according to each site requirement provided in Attachment A

3.3.2. Each kiosk shall include a printing system for patient queuing ticket printout

3.3.3. System must have multiple check-in categories for separation of patient into multiple queues (i.e., blood draw, drop off, research, no orders)

3.3.4. Kiosk/check-in device can allow patients to check-in manually using alphanumeric characters

3.3.5. Patient check-in information will be visible to staff after patient self-check-in

3.3.6. System includes number of freestanding floor kiosks according to each site requirement provided in Attachment A

3.3.7. Patient queuing ticket available immediately upon patient check-in

3.3.8. Ticket printed must include sequential number assigned to the patient

3.3.9. Ticket printout is customizable by the end user

3.3.10. Must include sufficient annual printer paper volumes to meet VISN 22 healthcare system requirements as per Attachment A, Tab 2. Site Requirements, column J - Estimated Annual Patient Volumes.

3.3.11. Includes all necessary power cords for a 110V operation

3.3.12. Kiosk/device can be sanitized with commonly used disinfectants used by healthcare settings to stop the spread of disease and contagions

3.3.13. Patient check-in Kiosk/device utilizes touch screen technology

3.4. Main Lobby Visual Display

3.4.1. System includes display monitor(s) in patient waiting areas for visual patient notification

3.4.2. VAGLA Activations Team will provide Monitor

3.4.3. Must include power cord/supply for 110V operation

3.5. Departmental Display Monitor

3.5.1. System includes display for departmental use to manage patient queuing assignments

3.5.2. VAGLA Activation Team will provide Monitor 

3.5.3. Must include power cord/supply for 110V operation

3.6. Signage

3.6.1. System must include digital signage displays for each work/draw station

3.6.2. Digital display of assigned numbers visible to patients in waiting area

3.6.3. Display will direct patient to appropriate work/draw station

3.7. Audible Notification

3.7.1. Adjustable audible alert in waiting area including installation of speakers in specified locations

3.8. Reports

3.8.1. Patient Wait Time report with details for each phase in the workflow (i.e., Transaction/Encounter time i.e., time spent with patient at each station)

3.8.2. Customizable patient satisfaction survey with detailed reports

3.8.3. Reports include number of overall encounters per day, per unique user, specific workstation, user, and/or draw station location

3.8.4. Remote monitoring of current wait times by location manager

3.8.5. Ability to customize reports by established user parameters

notices.title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source: SockPuppet
notices.agency_path: STATE, DEPARTMENT OF.STATE, DEPARTMENT OF.ACQUISITIONS - AQM MOMENTUM
notices.description_text:
The Department of State (DOS), Bureau of Global Acquisitions (GA) intends to award a sole source purchase order to DH Technologies, Inc. located at 161 Fort Evans Rd. NE, Suite 255, Leesburg, VA 20176. In accordance with FAR 13.101(b), contracting officers may solicit a procurement with a total value under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold from a single source based on a determination and findings that only one source is reasonably available, such as in the case of a brand name requirement.

The proposed acquisition is to support the Department of State's Bureau of Diplomatic Security (DS), Office of Open Source Intelligence (DS/TIA/OSN) to acquire the SockPuppet-brand managed, non-attributable online research environment, delivered as a service, to support authorized open-source intelligence, online investigations, and related research. OSN has identified SockPuppet as the only product known to the Office that provides all of the required capabilities as a single, integrated, managed service under one contract. Other products provide partial subsets of these capabilities, but none provides the full combination required, no other product can be modified to meet the requirement, and no combination of available products can be assembled into an equivalent capability at acceptable cost, risk, and timeline. Therefore, this is a brand name requirement for SockPuppet specifically.

DH Technologies has been identified as the only authorized reseller that has completed SockPuppet's formal reseller training program and is properly equipped to sell and support the full SockPuppet service suite.

A request for more information, or a copy of the solicitation will not be considered an affirmative response to this Notice. Telephone responses or inquires to this Notice will not be accepted.

GA will consider written responses received electronically no later than Friday, September 4, 2026 at 3:00pm ET to Elizabeth Surette (SuretteEK@state.gov). Responses must include evidence that clearly shows your company is capable of providing the content described in this notice. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no written response is received by the aforementioned deadline that clearly demonstrates an ability to meet all requirements, and that is more advantageous to the Government, DOS will make an award on a sole source basis to DH Technologies, Inc.

The Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. All costs associated with responding to this notice will be solely at the expense of the interested party.

The Naval Air Warfare Center Training Systems Division (NAWCTSD) intends to negotiate, on a sole source basis, a contract for the Integrated Tactical Trainer (ITT) 2B & 2C Operating Systems Updates and Modifications to include the following:

 The current procurement includes operating systems updates (i.e. Windows 11 and Red Hat Enterprise License) and system modifications to the ITT-2B and 2C inclusive of the design, fabrication, procurement, delivery, installation, integration, configuration, technical documentation, test, modernization, and concurrency of the Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) Independence Variant ITT devices 20B14 SN1 and 20B14 SN2 installed in Naval Station San Diego, CA.

 This procurement specifically involves: (1) LCS trainer support (i.e. hardware, software, documentation) as required to retain training capability throughout its lifecycle; (2) The integration of the ITTs with the tech refreshed Common Mission Package Trainers (CMPTs) and the Multi-Data Link Management System (MDLMS), (3) Configuration management to ensure all software suites are properly tracked and updated; (4) Installation of latest version of Windows, Windows Server, and Red Hat Enterprise License (RHEL) to meet Department of War (DoW) Cyber directive; (4) Installation and integration of VSHIP 10 to be compatible with latest version of Windows; (5) Converting existing scenario files to VSHIP 10; (6) Removal of Splunk platform and replacing with Aria Cybersecurity to be concurrent with the ship; (7) Upgrade existing hypervisors to align with tactical Total Ship Computing Environment (TSCE) modernization solution (i.e. ESXi ver.7 u3); (8) Update After Action Review (AAR) hardware and software for mission debrief; (9) Update the Video Display System to operate with the new OS and VSHIP 10; (10) Install VSHIP 10 on the CMPTs and ensure they are still functional with ITTs.

The contract is planned for General Dynamics Mission System (GDMS) (Cage Code 3CX85) of Pittsfield, MA under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." 

GDMS is the only source with the requisite knowledge, experience, and technical expertise to provide the LCS Operating Systems (OS) upgrades and modifications without an unacceptable delay to the Fleet. A major component of the LCS upgrade is the integration of the VSHIP with the updated operating systems and tactical systems equipment. GDMS is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) for the ITT-2B and 2C Independence Variant devices 20B14 SN1 and 20B14 SN2 installed in Naval Station San Diego, CA and the only source capable of meeting the form, fit, and function requirements in a timely manner. In addition, GDMS is the sole provider of VSHIP licenses and has the expertise to integrate VSHIP with the updated OS and tactical systems equipment. GDMS has access to internal data as the OEM of the VSHIP and would not need to wait for the final data deliverable to begin proposal and development efforts for the LCS upgrades. A learning curve exists where the architecture/interface integrates component software into the comprehensive training environment. The LCS upgrades will address interfaces to all currently established systems including Bridge Navigation, Engineering, Command/Control, and Combat training systems, which integrate with Surface Warfare (SUW) and Mine Warfare (MIW/MCM) Common Mission Package Trainer (CMPT) capabilities. These training systems provide practical application training in navigation, ship handling, and combat scenarios in support of U.S. Navy (USN) curricula, and meet Navy Training System Plan (NTSP) requirements for LCS Train to Qualify (T2Q) watch stander and Type Commander (TYCOM) Certification team training. All of the above mentioned systems are dedicated systems with constantly evolving interfaces that will be delivered as part of the upgraded operating systems and modifications. As the OEM, developer, and integrator of the VSHIP and the LCS Independent Variant ITT-2B and 2C devices for the LCS ships, GDMS will solely have the expertise interfacing these systems through the experience and knowledge gained integrating them onboard the ships. GDMS is the only contractor capable of delivering this functional upgrade on the ITT-2B and 2C in the established timeframe required to meet concurrency.

A single award is anticipated prior to April 2027. The anticipated contract value for this procurement is $8M total.

Ongoing market research performed by the Government supports there does not exist a commercially available item or non-developmental item to satisfy the Government's requirement.

This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. It is a notice in accordance with RFO 5.101 outlining the Government's intent to contract on a sole source basis with GDMS. Interested sources are solicited to provide their written technical capabilities. Written response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. Interested sources must submit detailed written technical capabilities to deliver the requirement. Detailed written capabilities must be submitted by email to Dr. Tina Daniels (tina.daniels4.civ@us.navy.mil) with a copy to Ms. Cynthia Armound (cynthia.d.armound.civ@us.navy.mil) in an electronic format that is compatible with Microsoft Office 2016 applications (MS Word), no later than close of business on Friday, September 11, 2026. Verbal submissions via phone will not be honored.

All information shall be furnished at no cost or obligation to the Government. Responses shall be limited to no more than TEN (10) pages. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. This notice is not to be considered a request for quotations or proposals. No solicitation document is available. No contract will be awarded on the basis of offers received in response to this notice, but will be used to determine if a comparable source is available and more advantageous to the Government. If no written challenge to this synopsis is received, a justification and approval (J&A) for other than full and open competition in accordance with the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) subpart 6.103-1 based on the rationale provided above will be initiated. If conducted as a sole source procurement, a separate synopsis will not follow. This synopsis will satisfy the intent of the requirements under RFO 5.101. In accordance with RFO 5.101(c)(4)(i), copies of the solicitation will be available upon request.
