notices.agency_path: COMMERCE, DEPARTMENT OF.NATIONAL OCEANIC AND ATMOSPHERIC ADMINISTRATION.DEPT OF COMMERCE NOAA
notices.description_text:
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's (NOAA) Acquisition and Grants Office, Eastern Acquisition Division-Kansas City intends to negotiate and award a Base plus four option year purchase order, on a sole source basis, under authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1, with GRAW Radiosondes GmbH & Co. KG for software support services for existing GRAW Radiosondes for the National Weather Service (NWS) Program Management Office in Silver Spring, MD.

Sole Source Justification: 

The sole source determination is based on NOAA's Sole Source Justification. Only one source is capable - GRAW Radiosondes GmbH & Co. KG is the only company that can make modifications to the source code necessary to identify, modify, and rectify potential issues. This GRAW Radiosondes GmbH & Co. KG brand name is essential to the requirement because the source code and internal architecture of GRAWMET are proprietary to the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). No other commercial software can process the unique data telemetry formats of the DFM-17 radiosonde or integrate with the existing MROS ground station hardware. Attempting to modify third­party software to meet these needs is not feasible, as it would require unauthorized access to proprietary GRAW protocols and would risk a critical gap in service. A disruption in support would prevent 55 sites from launching radiosondes, leading to a loss of mission-critical atmospheric data essential for tracking hurricanes and other significant weather patterns. Therefore, GRAW Radiosondes GmbH & Co. KG is the only source capable of providing the required maintenance and security updates necessary to ensure the continued reliability of the NWS upper-air observation network. 

This pre-solicitation notice is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation package is available. However, firms that believe they can fully meet the government's requirements may submit substantiating documentation or a request for additional information in writing to the (Contract Specialist) within 15 days after publication of this pre-solicitation notice. Such requests and documentation will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the government not to conduct a competitive procurement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this pre-solicitation notice.

notices.title: Sources Sought Notice for Information Technology Client Services for the U.S. Naval Academy
notices.agency_path: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NAVSUP.NAVSUP GLOBAL LOGISTICS SUPPORT.NAVSUP FLC NORFOLK.NAVSUP FLT LOG CTR NORFOLK
notices.description_text:
Sources Sought Notice for Information Technology Client Services for the U.S. Naval Academy

The Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Fleet Logistics Center Norfolk (FLCN) is issuing this RFI as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support the requirement for a non-personal services contract to provide Information Technology (IT) support in the Information Technology Services Division (ITSD) at the United States Naval Academy (USNA) and surrounding Annapolis Area Complex (AAC). The personnel will be working in the Client Services Department of ITSD with occasional work conducted for other departments within ITSD. 

A single award, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) purchase order action under NAICS code 541519 with a size standard of $34M is anticipated.

Subject to FAR Clause 52.215-3, entitled "Solicitation for Information of Planning Purpose," this announcement constitutes a sources sought synopsis for written information only. This is not a solicitation and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. This request for information (RFI) notice is not to be construed in any way as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response.

Please see the attached performance work statement for full details.

PROGRAM BACKGROUND 

The USNA ITSD provides voice, video and data communications service and support for selected organizations located throughout the Annapolis Area Complex (AAC). These offerings are a critical component of USNA ITSD's centrally managed and fully integrated responsibilities encompassing all AAC information technology. The USNA ITSD supports approximately 7,000 clients located throughout the 650-acre AAC and an additional 400 clients at the Naval Academy Preparatory School (NAPS) located in Newport, Rhode Island. IT on-site support requirements for NAPS are covered under a separate contract. 

The ITSD Client Services Department is responsible for providing IT support to all clients. Tier 1 support consists of receiving requests for service, providing telephone assistance in resolving reported problems, and tracking requests in a ticket management system from receipt of call to completion of service. Tier 2 support is invoked when telephone consultation proves inadequate to resolve the user's issues and consists of the resolution of a trouble ticket requiring a visit by information technology specialists to the client's work site or vice versa. Both Tier 1 and Tier 2 support also utilize remote assistance by connecting to client workstations in order to facilitate delivering services to customers within the AAC. 

IT support is accomplished by a blended team that consists of both government Full-Time Employees (FTEs) and contract personnel. Team members identify and deliver situation-specific information technology support services satisfying discipline-specific client needs (e.g. learning space operation and maintenance, technology-curriculum integration and coordination, faculty/staff education, rudimentary systems administration, etc.). 

Meanwhile, additional centralized team members are integrated into a fully functional Information Technology Service Center (ITSC) and maintenance facility located in USNA's Ward Hall. These centralized facilities coordinate critical common service and support activities (e.g. routine client information technology account administration, introductory client familiarization, general client walk-in assistance, building access for Ward Hall, software inventory and issuance, security and virus prevention updates, information technology asset management, information technology equipment troubleshooting and repair, etc.) to achieve benefits from scale economies at the enterprise level. The centralized facilities also provide an alternative entry point for resolution of client needs. Successful service outcomes require close cooperation and coordination between both provider groups which are facilitated through periodic discussion forums and routinely tracked using Government-provided Web Help Desk (WHD) software and regularly scheduled summary reports. Use of the ticketing system WHD is subject to change during the life of the contract. 

The Academic Technical Support Center (ATSC) is centrally located near academic buildings and primarily supports the academic faculty and staff. 

Hopper Hall support will support Computer Science, Cyber Science, and other departments within the Math and Sciences Division. Their computer systems are primarily Linux within classrooms and labs.

Contractor support is required for a base period of 12 months and 4 additional option years. 

REQUIRED CAPABILITIES 

The Contractor shall provide services in support of the areas specified in Program Background (above). Specific tasks are outlined in the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) attached to this announcement (Attachment 1). If your organization has the potential capacity to perform these contract services, please provide the following information: 1) Organization name, address, email address, web site address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. 

[Note: In accordance with FAR 10.001(b), the Government is requesting potential sources to submit only the minimum information necessary.]

The Government will evaluate the capability submissions to ascertain potential market capacity to: 1) provide services consistent, in scope and scale, with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated; 2) secure and apply the full range of corporate financial, human capital, and technical resources required to successfully perform similar requirements; 3) implement a successful project management plan that includes: compliance with tight program schedules; cost containment; meeting and tracking performance; hiring and retention of key personnel and risk mitigation; and 4) provide services under a performance based service acquisition contract. 

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: 

All contractor employees must obtain a favorable determination of eligibility to occupy a National Security position with access to IT-Level II information only based on a Tier 3 investigation by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM). All contractors must obtain a CAC. Employment will be contingent on the favorable adjudication of the Tier 3 investigation by the DODCAF. Additional reports may be requested during the course of employment as well.

Currently approximately nine (9) months is the standard service time for completion of a Tier 3 investigation by OPM. Contractor employees shall have a current Tier 3 Investigation with OPM, or Tier 3 investigation submitted and favorable FBI fingerprint results and be in possession of a CAC prior to starting work at USNA. 

ELIGIBILITY 

The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is 541519 - Other Computer Related Services with a Small Business Size Standard of $34.M. The Product Service Code is D307, It and Telecom - It Strategy and Architecture. Only SBA Certified Hub-Zone and Women Owned Small Businesses are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION AND SUBMISSION DETAILS (CAPABILITIES STATEMENT) 

A draft Performance Work Statement of (PWS) which entails Personnel Qualifications and Description are attached for review (Attachment 1). 

Interested parties are requested to submit a capabilities statement of no more than fifteen (15) pages in length in Times New Roman font of not less than 10 font size. The deadline for response to this request is no later than 4 pm, EST 7 September 2026. 

This documentation must address at a minimum the following items:

1.) What type of work has your company performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement?

2.) Can or has your company managed a task of this nature? If so, please provide details.

3.) Can or has your company managed a team of subcontractors before? If so, provide details.

4.) What specific technical skills does your company possess which ensure capability to perform the tasks?

5.) Please note that under a Small-Business Set-Aside, in accordance with FAR 52.219-14, the small business prime must perform at least 50% of the work themselves in terms of the cost of performance. Provide an explanation of your company's ability to perform at least 50% of the tasking described in this PWS for the base period as well as the option periods.

6.) Provide a statement including current small/large business status and company profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history, office locations, DUNs number, etc.

7.) Respondents to this notice also must indicate whether they qualify as an SBA certified HUBZone.

8.) Include in your response your ability to meet the requirements in the Facility and Safeguarding requirements.

The estimated period of performance consists of one twelve month base and four twelve month option periods.

The contract type is anticipated to be Firm Fixed Price.

The proposed contract is anticipated to include tasking that would be accomplished by labor categories that are subject to the Service Contract Act or a collective bargaining agreement.

Your response to this RFI, including any capabilities statement, shall be electronically submitted via email in either Microsoft Word or Portable Document Format (PDF) to Mrs. Megan Evans at megan.m.evans18.civ@us.navy.mil, and Mr. Gilbert Dobison at gilbert.k.dobison.civ@us.navy.mil

All data received in response to this RFI that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government.

No phone calls will be accepted. 

(Attachment 1) Performance Work Statement (PWS) - USNA PWS.pdf

notices.description_text:
This is a Sources Sought Notice issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government is seeking capability statements from commercial sources to determine market availability, technical feasibility, and potential small business set-aside avenues (SDVOSB) for an Enterprise Patient Elopement & Wander Management System.

Please submit the following:
Interested contractors shall submit a Capability Statement detailing:
Company Information: Legal Business Name, SAM.gov UEI/CAGE Code, Point of Contact, and Socioeconomic Status under NAICS 541519.
Technical Capability: Brief narrative demonstrating capability to deliver, install, and service an enterprise patient elopement platform. Indicate if providing brand-name products (e.g., GuardRFID, Stanley Healthcare/Huggies/WanderGuard) or equal custom solutions.
Contract Vehicles: List any existing GWAC or FSS contracts (e.g., GSA MAS, VA FSS, SEWP) your firm currently holds that cover these supplies/services.
4. Response Guidelines
Response Deadline: 9/11/26 3:00 p.m. 
Submission Format: PDF via email to cheryl.roberts2@va.gov 
Subject Line: Sources Sought Response - Patient Elopement System - [Company Name]
Note: The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting information in response to this notice.

Statement of Need: Patient Elopement Prevention System, Wilmington VA Medical Center, Wilmington Delaware

Background:
Patient elopement represents a significant safety risk within healthcare facilities, particularly for vulnerable populations such as those with cognitive impairment, mental health conditions, or those at risk of harm to themselves or others. Elopement incidents can result in emotional distress, bodily harm, or even fatalities, and place a legal and reputational burden on the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).

Need Statement:
The VA Wilmington VAMC requires a comprehensive Patient Elopement Prevention System to proactively mitigate the risk of unauthorized patient departures ( elopements ), ensure the safety of patients, and comply with The Joint Commission and other regulatory requirements related to patient monitoring, safety, and reporting.

Objectives:

Prevention: Reduce the incidence of patient elopement from inpatient and specialty care units.
Real-time Monitoring: Enable real-time location tracking and immediate alerts to staff if a patient at risk attempts to exit designated safe zones.
Rapid Response: Provide timely notification to appropriate response personnel to intervene and prevent patient harm.
Audit and Reporting: Facilitate post-incident reviews, trend analysis, and meet documentation/internal audit requirements.
Scope:
The anticipated system shall include, but not be limited to:

Removal and proper disposal of the existing patient elopement prevention system and associated hardware in accordance with VA environmental and information security policies
Installation and deployment of the new patient elopement prevention system
Wearable tags or wristbands for at-risk patients
Fixed and/or portable monitoring devices covering all potential exit points
Integration with existing VA IT and security infrastructure
Real-time notification to nursing stations and mobile devices
Secure logging and reporting features
Staff training and maintenance support
Conclusion:
The implementation of a Patient Elopement Prevention System will enhance the standard of care at Wilmington VAMC, protect Veteran patients, and ensure regulatory compliance. Procuring this system is essential to upholding the VA mission of providing safe, high-quality healthcare.

notices.title: MasterCAM on Athena
notices.agency_path: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE
notices.description_text:
AFSC/PZIOA, on behalf of the 76 CMXG, intends to issue a sole source award to Phillips Federal Division for a MasterCAM on Athena. MasterCAM provides a comprehensive CAD/CAM solution for diverse machining needs, offering powerful tool paths and simulation to optimize efficiency and reduce errors. Its versatility, industry-leading features, and strong support network make it a valuable investment for complex manufacturing challenges. MasterCAM is actively used in DoD training program, aerospace/defense manufacturing, and procurement contracts. It is embedded in both education pipelines and production workflows for defense parts, and is procured directly by DoD agencies, confirming its significant role in U.S. defense manufacturing. In MasterCAM, "React" is a feature used in the Athena module (part of MasterCAM's CAM automation and workflow tools) to automatically respond to changes in the machining process by adjusting operations, geometries, or toolpaths without manual re-programming. MasterCAM is actively used in DoD training programs, aerospace/defense manufacturing, and procurement contracts. It is embedded in both educational pipelines (like Watervliet Arsenal) and production workflows for defense parts, and is procured directly by DoD agencies, confirming its significant role in U.S. defense manufacturing. 

List of Materials with specific part numbers and specifications is attached. 

The Government has determined that Phillips Federal Division is the only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisify agency requirements. 

This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole source basis under the statutory authority of FAR 6.302-1 - Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Unless stated herein, no additional information is available. Requests for the same will be disregarded. Responsible interested parties may submit a capability statement in which they identify their interest and capability to respond to this requirement, if received within seven calendar days after the date of this publication of this notice. The Government will consider all information received by the response date. notices.agency_path: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE ARMY.USACE.NWD.W071 ENDIST PORTLAND
notices.description_text:
THIS IS A SPECIAL NOTICE PREPARED IN ACCORDANCE WITH FEDERAL ACQUISITION REGULATION (FAR) SUBPART 5.2 "SYNOPSES OF PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTIONS"

NAICS 541519, Other Computer Related Services

Response Deadline: 1 September 2026

The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Portland District (NWP) intends to negotiate/award a firm-fixed price (FFP) service, single source procurement to North Coast Electric Company for Tech Connect Support Services at The Dalles Lock and Dam, Oregon.

REASON FOR SOLE SOURCE ACQUISITION:

The statutory authority for this non-competitive acquisition is 10 USC § 3204(a)(1), RFO FAR 12.102(a), Soliciting from a single source for commercial purchases not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold.

The purpose is to provide Tech Connect Support Services at The Dalles Lock and Dam, Oregon.

Background: The required Tech Connect Support Services at The Dalles Lock and Dam are specifically for Rockwell Automation brand hardware, software and support products. The Dalles Dam Project currently has (59 each) Allen-Bradley programmable logic controllers (manufactured by Rockwell Automation) currently in service that require the use of Allen-Bradley products, including software updates. This requires a current Tech Connect support contract.

Justification: North Coast Electric Company is the only appointed Allen-Bradley distributor authorized to sell Allen-Bradley Standard Controls, Drives, PLC/MMI and Rockwell Software products, along with related services, in the geographic area in which The Dalles Lock and Dam is located. Factory products and sales support are made available only through the local authorized distributor, North Coast Electric Company. No other company is a local authorized distributor, and no other company can provide these services to The Dalles Lock and Dam.

Impact: Continued Tech Connect Services are mandatory. Without this purchase, damage or failure to critical equipment that is controlled by Allen-Bradley hardware and software is likely to result due to the inability to properly maintain the Allen-Bradley products at The Dalles Lock and Dam.

The Government intends to solicit North Coast Electric Company directly for this project on or around 3 September 2026. At this time, a solicitation does not exist. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency.

*NO PHONE INQUIRIES, PLEASE.

CAPABILITY STATEMENT SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

(PLEASE REVIEW ALL BELOW)

Point of Contact name, email address and phone number, CAGE code and DUNS number (if available);

In the event that the organization is a small business, please state the category of small business, such as 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB/VOSB, Women-Owned Small Business.

The Government will evaluate the capabilities of an interested party based on their ability to provide the required Tech Connect Services.

Send responses, labeled as "W9127N26QA091 – The Dalles Tech Connect Support Services" to the following:

David.C.Boone@usace.army.mil

General Services Administration (GSA), Assisted Acquisition Services (AAS) is releasing a Request for Information (RFI) on behalf of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Administration (CISA). As provided by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 10.001 (GSA Class Deviation Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO)-2025-10), industry engagement serves as a market research tool used by AAS to gauge industry interest, assess potential commercial/industry approaches, identify factors that could shape the acquisition strategy, inform future acquisition planning, promote competition, and improve the quality of proposals. The Government will request only the minimum information necessary, and all responses will be used solely for market research purposes. Any response to this RFI or information submitted by an interested Industry Partner to the Government will not be shared with any other Industry Partner. Participation in the RFI process is strictly voluntary.

This RFI does NOT constitute a Request for Proposal and is not to be construed as a commitment, implied or otherwise, by the Government that a procurement action will be issued. A response to this RFI is not a request to be added to a bidders list or to receive a copy of a solicitation. No entitlement to payment of direct or indirect costs or charges by the Government will arise as a result of the submission of the requested information. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this RFI and any follow-up information requests. The Government may not respond to any specific questions or comments in response to this RFI or information provided as a result of this request. This information will be used for market research only.

The Government is particularly interested in determining the information, documents, or similar data that industry would need to facilitate a bid/no bid decision and in the availability and applicability of commercial products and services to meet the requirements of the CISA Strategic Cyber Tools Buying requirement.

**Additionally, the Government welcomes respondents to identify any questions, assumptions, concerns, or recommendations related to this requirement that were not specifically addressed in this RFI. Respondents are encouraged to provide insight into areas where additional clarification or market research may be beneficial. This information may be used to further inform the Government's acquisition strategy and requirement definition. The Government may also use this feedback to develop discussion topics for a potential Industry Day, one-on-one Market Analysis Discussions (MAD) sessions, or other future market research activities. Submission of questions or assumptions does not guarantee that they will be addressed publicly or that a follow-on engagement will occur.

notices.agency_path: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE AIR FORCE.AIR FORCE MATERIEL COMMAND.AIR FORCE LIFE CYCLE MANAGEMENT CENTER.DIGITAL.FA8730  KESSEL RUN AFLCMC/HBBK
notices.description_text:
Update (24 August 2026):

The Anticipated Milestone schedule has been updated. No response to this updated announcement is required from interested vendors.

Upcoming Anticipated Milestones:

Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) Release - September 2026 

Industry Engagement on Draft RFP - September/October 2026 

Final Request for Proposal (RFP) Release - January 2027 

Contract Award (Estimated) - August 2027

Announcement:

The Air Operations Center Program Office, Kessel Run Division, Portfolio Acquisition Executive Command, Control, Communications, and Battle Management (PAE C3BM/C3C) is initiating market research to identify and explore cutting-edge technologies and innovative approaches for the modernization of the Air Operations Center (AOC) Weapon System. The AOC is the senior command and control element for the Joint Force Air Component Commander, responsible for planning, executing, and assessing air, space, and cyberspace operations. 

Statement of Need 

The AOC Weapon System AN/USQ-163 Falconer is a critical component of our nation's defense, enabling commanders to make rapid, informed decisions in complex and dynamic environments. The current sustainment and modernization contract FA8730-22-F-0071 was awarded to SAIC. As we look to the future, we are seeking to build upon these efforts and identify new and emerging technologies that can further enhance the AOC's capabilities. 

We are particularly interested in solutions that address the following opportunities and risks: 

Opportunities: 

 
 Integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning to accelerate decision-making. 

 

 
 Enhanced data fusion and visualization from disparate sources. 

 

 
 Advanced cybersecurity measures to protect against emerging threats. 

 

 
 Cloud-native architectures for increased agility, scalability, and resilience 

 

Risks: 

 
 The ever-evolving cyber threat landscape. 

 

 
 The challenge of integrating legacy systems with modern technologies. 

 

Industry Engagement 

This Program Announcement is the first step in a broader engagement with industry for market research purposes. A Request for Information (RFI) is linked to this announcement as of 26 February 2026. Based on the responses received, we anticipate holding a series of future forums, including: 

 
 Virtual One-on-Ones: To discuss your proposed solutions in more detail. 

 

 
 Technology Demonstrations: To see your innovative technologies in action. 

 

 
 Industry Roundtables: To foster a collaborative discussion on the future of the AOC Weapon System. 

 

 
 Program Manager Q&As: To get the specific answers you need to better understand the level of effort and work required to perform 

 

Below is a tentative schedule of events for the Program Office – these dates are subject to change: 

Anticipated Milestone and Projected Start Timeline (Updated as of 24 August 2026)

Request for Information (RFI) Release - February 2026 

Initial Industry Engagement & Feedback - March 2026 

Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) Release - September 2026 

Industry Engagement on Draft RFP - September/October 2026 

Final Request for Proposal (RFP) Release - January 2027 

Contract Award (Estimated) - August 2027

--

We look forward to hearing from the innovative leaders in the industry and working together to shape the future of the AOC Weapon System.

Any information submitted by respondents to this special notice is strictly voluntary. This is neither a Request for Proposal nor a Notice of Contract Action (NOCA). This is a program announcement for market research purposes. Responses to the notice will not be returned. Respondents are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice or upcoming RFI; all costs associated with responding to this notice will be solely at the interested parties' expense. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on this notice. 

 

Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to provide feedback with respect to any information submitted. To the maximum extent possible, please submit non-proprietary information. Any proprietary information submitted should be identified as such and will be handled accordingly and protected from disclosure. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. The Government shall not be liable for damages related to proprietary information that is not properly identified. 

 

Any submissions in response to this notice constitutes consent for that submission to be reviewed by Government personnel, Federally Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC) Contractor employees, and Advisory & Assistance Services (A&AS) Contractor employees supporting the Air Operations Center Program Office -- unless the respondent clearly objects in writing to the release of this information to FFRDC and/or A&AS Contractor employees supporting PAE C3BM/C3C in a cover letter accompanying the respondent's submission. All Government and Department of Defense (DoD) contractor personnel reviewing responses understand their responsibility for proper use and protection from unauthorized disclosure of proprietary information.

notices.title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE
notices.agency_path: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.USMC.MARCOR SYSCOM.COMMANDER
notices.description_text:
NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE

Contract Number (Current): M67854-19-D-7614

Anticipated Action: Sole-Source Contract Modification (Ordering Period Extension and Ceiling Increase)

(1) Point of Contact

The primary point of contact and Contracting Officer for this action is detailed below:

Contracting Officer:

Ms. Renée S. Stahl

Branch Head – Contracts, PM LI2S-MC / ITCC / PAE MS

Marine Corps Systems Command

701 S. Courthouse Rd.

Arlington, VA 22204

Contracting Activity Address:

Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS)

Program Manager, Logistics Integrated Information Solutions – Marine Corps (PM LI2S-MC)

Product Manager, Global Combat Support System – Marine Corps (PdM GCSS-MC)

105 Tech Parkway

Stafford, VA 22556

(2) Set-Asides

No set-asides are applicable to this proposed contract action. This action is a sole-source modification to the incumbent contractor, CACI Federal, Inc., under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1). Due to the highly specialized nature of the legacy system sustainment and the immediate transition requirements, small business set-asides (total, partial, or local area) under Part 19 or Part 26 are not feasible for this transition phase.

(3) Codes for Services or Supplies

The following classification codes identify the services to be provided:

 Product Service Code (PSC): DA01 – IT and Telecom - Business Application/Application Development Support Services (Support - Professional)

 North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 541512 – Computer Systems Design Services

(iv) Technical Data Requirements

No technical data package or separate solicitation documents will be issued for this sole-source modification. Technical data regarding the internal, highly customized architecture of the legacy Global Combat Support System – Marine Corps (GCSS-MC) is proprietary to the government and the incumbent systems integrator. If prospective offerors require additional non-proprietary technical information to submit a capability statement, they may submit a written request to the Contracting Officer listed in Section (1).

(v) Equitable Adjustments for Construction Contracts

Not Applicable. The proposed acquisition is for Information Technology (IT) and systems engineering services. It does not involve the award of a construction contract.

(vi) Submission of Proposals by Responsible Sources

All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals; however, the Government will consider all capability statements received within fifteen (15) days of the publication of this notice. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

(vii) Noncompetitive Contract Action Justification

Intended Source:

CACI Federal, Inc.

14370 Newbrook Drive

Chantilly, VA 20151-4206

Justification and Lack of Competition:

PAE MS / Marine Corps Systems Command intends to execute a sole-source modification to extend the ordering period by up to three years (ending 25 December 2029, or upon successful operational cut-over, whichever occurs first) and increase the contract ceiling by $150,000,000.00.

The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by RFO 6.103-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements."

Competition is lacking because this transitional phase requires highly specialized systems integration, database engineering, and business process reengineering (BPR) services that cannot be unbundled from the active operational sustainment of the legacy GCSS-MC environment. Over its lifecycle, the legacy GCSS-MC E-Business Suite (EBS) architecture has undergone non-standard, extensive customization, resulting in a tightly coupled, bespoke data schema that deviates from commercial baselines.

The incumbent systems integrator possesses exclusive institutional knowledge of these system-specific idiosyncrasies, ongoing API integrations, and non-standard data tables. Onboarding a new vendor to perform these critical services during the sunset window of the legacy platform would inject unacceptable schedule delays (estimated at 12 to 18 months) to account for procurement lead time, contractor transition, and reverse-engineering of the legacy codebase. Under RFO 6.103-1(c)(2)(ii), such delays would directly compromise total unit readiness across the operating forces, degrade the entire GCSS-MC logistics enterprise, and disrupt the transition to the future Logistics Chain Management System (LCMS).

(viii) Qualification Requirements

There are no pre-established, formal qualification requirements (per RFO Part 9) that an offeror or its service must meet to be eligible for award. However, any interested source must demonstrate immediate, expert-level capability to sustain the highly customized GCSS-MC EBS environment and execute complex database cleansing and extraction without causing operational downtime.

(4) Description of Services

The Marine Corps requires continuous, uninterrupted operations of GCSS-MC—the Accountable Property System of Record (APSR) for the Marine Corps supporting over 22,000 enterprise users and 75+ worldwide locations—while preparing the system's data and structures for transition to the future LCMS. This action will provide:

 The baseline engineering and labor required to keep the legacy GCSS-MC EBS operational, maintain strict system availability and performance standards, and ensure continuous logistics support in both garrison and deployed environments. This also includes sustaining the GCSS-MC Mobile Training Suites in their current configuration to support Fleet Marine Force training requirements.

 Encompass the highly technical, labor-intensive mapping of the customized EBS baseline to the LCMS Phase 1 data schema. This includes the identification and remediation of non-standard data tables and bespoke RICECPW objects accumulated over years of production; extraction and transformation of logistics, supply, maintenance, and financial data in compliance with GAAP, SFFAS 3, and SFFAS 29; and preparing the legacy structures for secure ingestion by the future Cloud-Based, Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) hosting environment.

Future-state LCMS architecture is designed to prevent vendor lock-in, and the LCMS System Integrator contract(s) are anticipated to be awarded via competition (anticipated in Q3FY27). This modification serves as the necessary, time-limited transition to enable that competitive future state.

notices.title: 7A20--Request for Information (RFI) - Industry Day
notices.agency_path: VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.TECHNOLOGY ACQUISITION CENTER NJ (36C10B)
notices.description_text:
The Department of Veterans Affairs
Request for Information Industry Day
September 09, 2026 September 10, 2026

Introduction 
This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research and acquisition 
planning purposes in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation
Overhaul (RFO) 8.4 and 10. This notice does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ),
Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB) or any commitment by the 
Government to issue a solicitation for or award a contract.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is conducting an Industry Day Event to assess the evolving observability marketplace. The VA operates at true enterprise scale with 550,000 end-user endpoints, 63,000+ monitored nodes, 853 unique services, and petabytes of data daily across hybrid cloud, on-premises, and multi-cloud environments. VA is seeking technical solutions that can combat significant platform challenges sustaining performance under ingestion and analytical workloads. 

VA is requesting interested vendors to respond to this RFI based on the details set forth below. Based on responses, VA will identify qualified vendors to participate for an in-person industry day in Austin, TX. Selection of qualified vendors for the purpose of this market research is at the Government s discretion.

VA will assess solutions based on:
How your product performs at true enterprise scale (ingestion, query performance, usability under load) 
Your Artificial Intelligence (AI) / agentic capabilities 
Your FedRAMP roadmap 
Your competitive positioning and market strategy

VA are seeking vendors in the following categories:
Network & Infrastructure Monitoring (NMS) platforms
Application Performance Monitoring (APM) solutions
AI Ops & Incident Management platforms
Enterprise Observability platforms that span multiple domains

Disclaimer
This notice does not in itself represent the issuance of a formal request for proposal/quote and is not intended to be taken as such. This is a Request for Information (RFI) only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Quotation, or a Request for Proposal. Do not submit a proposal or a quote. This market research is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation nor does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI. You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI. Any contract that might be awarded based on information received or derived from this market research will be the outcome of a competitive process. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI.

Step 1 RFI Submission 
Vendors shall respond by September 02, 2026, with their interest and literature to:
Chantel.Bass@va.gov, Kodi.Kirchofner@va.gov 
Email Subject Line: Response to RFI Number 36C10B26Q0777

Literature & Technical Specifications
Vendors shall submit technical specifications and supporting literature, not to exceed 30 pages that details:
Architecture overview (collector/agent model, scalability approach)
Performance benchmarks at scale (node count, event throughput, query latency) AI/agentic capabilities roadmap 
FedRAMP certification status and timeline
Deployment/integration complexity
Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM)
Connection to resellers including Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) and Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB)
Existing Government procurement vehicles

3.2 Attendee Details
Vendors shall provide an attendance list to include names, titles, and point of contact information. A maximum of five team members may attend, including at a minimum a Program/Project Manager (PM) and a Technical Subject Matter Expert (SME), remaining attendees are at the vendor s discretion. 

Identified Qualified Vendors
After reviewing the provided details, the Government will invite qualified vendors to participate in the industry day. Vendor pre-loaded scenario, presentation, and technical specifications shall be submitted by September 07, 2026. Responses shall be submitted electronically to:
Chantel.Bass@va.gov, Kodi.Kirchofner@va.gov 
Email Subject Line: Industry Day Briefing for RFI Number 36C10B26Q0777

Pre-Event Technical Briefing (Optional)
Vendors may request a 30-minute call with VA Technical Team to align on demo objectives. Pre-events must be scheduled prior to the Industry Day Event.

Event Details

Date: September 9, 2026 September 10, 2026

Location: The Department of Veterans Affairs 
Austin Information Technology Center (AITC) 
1615 Woodward Street, Austin, TX 78772

VA Attendees: VA Enterprise Command Center Director, Executive Leadership, CNS. Observability Manager, Technology Acquisition Center representation

Format: Full vendor presentations + Q&A + interactive panels

Property Instructions: The AITC building is a highly secure facility. Vendors are required to enter through the gated entrance, with parking in a visitor area. Only pre-authorized individuals from identified Vendors can access the building where they will undergo screening via metal detectors. 

Response Instructions
Each vendor will be allotted a 55-minute session structured as follows:
Opening (5 min): Your company/product positioning 
Live Demo of Pre-loaded Scenario (35 min): Walk through your scale demo, showcase performance, discuss architecture decisions 
AI/Agentic & Competitive Story (10 min): Where you're headed, FedRAMP strategy, unique value vs. competitors 
Q&A (10 min): Direct questions from VA decision makers
Transition (5 min): Escort vendor participant out

Pre-loaded Demon Scenario and Presentation
Vendors shall load a realistic VA-scale environment into their product/solution.

Minimum Requirements
At least 10,000+ monitored nodes/devices/services (more if feasible)
Multiple cloud environments represented (AWS, Azure, GCP if supported)
Real-world data patterns and performance characteristics
Pre-built dashboards showing service/application health

If a full VA-scale pre-load is not feasible, provide a representative scenario demonstrating your platform's ability to: 
Ingest and process high-volume metric/event data without degradation 
Perform complex queries and anomaly detection without slowdown
Support federated/distributed architecture if applicable

Vendors are highly encouraged to come to the table with engaging demonstrations under realistic conditions over relying on slide deck presentations.

Recommended Interested Sources:
SolarWinds
Dynatrace
LogicMonitor
PagerDuty
Other NMS vendors (Cisco, Kentik, Arista, others)
APM vendors (New Relic, Elastic APM, Datadog, others)
AIOps/Incident Management platforms (Splunk/Moogsoft, Atlassian,Incident.io, others)

Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability (JWCC) Next, now known as JWCC Unified Cloud Marketplace (UCM), will function as a single, unified solution that supports the consumption of all provisionally authorized (PA) cloud service offerings (CSOs) from approved cloud service providers (CSPs)—not limited to the current hyperscalers. To achieve this efficiently while preserving security, compliance, and operational integrity, the solution will be structured as follows:

 
 Tier 1 – Hyperscalers: Core infrastructure and platform services from established large-scale CSPs.

 

 
 Tier 2 – Everything-as-a-Service (XaaS): Includes Software-as-a-Service (SaaS), Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS), and non-hyperscale Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS).

 

 
 Tier 3 – Commercial Innovators & Small Businesses: Innovative, agile, and non-traditional cloud offerings from emerging providers and small businesses that meet PA standards.

 

This approach will create a comprehensive marketplace that promotes competition, accelerates access to cutting-edge capabilities, and ensures qualified industry partners can participate equitably.

notices.title: Integrated Tactical Trainer (ITT) 2B & 2C Operating Systems Updates and Modifications
notices.agency_path: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEPT OF THE NAVY.NAVAIR.NAVAIR NAWC TSD.NAWC TRAINING SYSTEMS DIV
notices.description_text:
INTRODUCTION

The Naval Air Warfare Center Training Systems Division (NAWCTSD) Orlando, FL intends to sole source the ITT-2B & 2C Operating Systems Updates and Modifications effort to General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS) (Cage Code 3CX85) of Pittsfield, MA under the authority of 10 USC 3204(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.

GDMS is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) for the ITT-2B and 2C Independence Variant devices 20B14 SN1 and 20B14 SN2 installed in Naval Station San Diego, CA and the only source capable of meeting the form, fit, and function requirements in a timely manner. In addition, GDMS is the sole provider of VSHIP licenses and has the expertise to integrate the VSHIP with the updated operating systems and tactical systems equipment. To comply with CD 2026-O0017 Revision 2 pursuant to RFO Part 6 DFARS PGI 206.103-170, the Government is seeking information on the availability of potential comparable sources to provide the ITT-2B & 2C Operating Systems Updates and Modifications to the fleet. Responses to this Sources Sought will be utilized to ensure no comparable source is available and more advantageous to the Government.

DISCLAIMER

THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY.

PLACES OF PERFORMANCE

Littoral Training Facility (LTF) Naval Station, San Diego, CA.

PROGRAM BACKGROUND

The Littoral Combat Ship (LCS-1) Integrated Tactical Trainer 1A (ITT-1A) was initially procured February 2003 and delivered to San Diego, CA via the LCS Preliminary Ship Design Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract, N00024-03-C-2311, through a series of modifications to CLIN 0012, Life Cycle Engineering & Support. Over a decade later in May 2016, the LCS-1 ITT-1B was procured under Firm-Fixed Priced (FFP) contract N61340-12-D-5111/0003, awarded to Lockheed Martin (LM) Rotary & Mission Systems (RMS) in the amount of $19.5M for a more commercially supportable design that integrated Crew Served Weapons (CSW) Trainers & Instructor Operator Stations (IOS) in Mayport, FL. In November 2019, LCS-1 ITT-1C was subsequently procured under contract N61340-20-C-0003 and awarded to LM RMS for concurrency with the former ITTs and modernization of ITTs A/B to include Mission Control Center (MCC) Training System upgrades, Engineering Training System (ETS) upgrades, and Bridge Wings.

Similarly, the initial Littoral Combat Ship (LCS-2) Integrated Tactical Trainer 2A (ITT-2A) was awarded July 2003 to Computer Sciences Corporation (CSC), currently known as General Dynamics Information Technology (GDIT), under NAVSEA contract N00024-03-C-2310, for the Independence Variant trainer located in San Diego, CA.

Likewise, over a decade later in September 2017, contract N61340-12-D-5105/N61340-17-F0112 was awarded to GDIT for the design, development, fabrication, integration, delivery, installation, configuration, technical documentation and testing of two new LCS ITT-2 trainers (ITT-2B & ITT-2C), as well as the retrofitting of the Legacy LCS ITT-2 trainer (ITT-2A) to maintain a consistent baseline with the new ITT-2 trainers in San Diego, CA.

As the sole Design Agent of the Independence Variant of the Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) and other related surface ship and maritime systems, General Dynamics Mission Systems was awarded contract N63394-24-C-0004 on 02 April 2024 by the NSWC PHD 03 Command for a period of performance ending 31 March 2027 for overall in-service engineering and life cycle support for Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Combat Systems and Intelligence (C5I) systems elements; and maintenance services of the Integrated Combat Management System (ICMS), its interfaces, software applications, and the networking environment hardware on the ITT-2B and 2C trainers located in San Diego, CA.

As such, General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS) is the only supplier of VSHIP licenses used on the Independent Variant LCS devices. The only way for the ITT-2B and 2C trainers to provide adequate training to the Fleet is to maintain the hardware (HW) and software (SW) profile which is used on the tactical platforms themselves. Deviating from shipboard components would eliminate any and all fidelity of the training the Fleet provides at LTF San Diego. GDMS remains the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) who can meet the form, fit, function requirements necessary for timely delivery and has the expertise to integrate the VSHIP with the updated operating systems and tactical systems equipment.

A single award is anticipated for execution before April 16, 2027. 

REQUIRED CAPABILITIES 

The Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) Integrated Tactical Trainers (ITTs) support individual and team training for the ship's crew. They provide unique and highly specialized functional training comprised of Bridge Navigation, Engineering, Command/Control, and Combat training systems and are capable of integrating with Surface Warfare (SUW) and Mine Warfare (MIW/MCM) Common Mission Package Trainer (CMPT) capabilities. These training systems provide practical application training in navigation, ship handling, and combat scenarios in support of U.S. Navy (USN) curricula, and meet Navy Training System Plan (NTSP) requirements for LCS Train to Qualify (T2Q) watch stander and Type Commander (TYCOM) Certification team training.

The current procurement includes operating systems updates (i.e. Windows 11 and Red Hat Enterprise License) and system modifications to the ITT-2B and 2C inclusive of the design, fabrication, procurement, delivery, installation, integration, configuration, technical documentation, test, modernization, and concurrency of the Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) Independence Variant ITT devices 20B14 SN1 and 20B14 SN2 installed in Naval Station San Diego, CA.

Respondents should clearly describe the following high-level capabilities:

 The method in which the respondent intends to obtain GDMS propriety data within a reasonable price and schedule.

 Demonstration of requisite LCS knowledge, experience, and technical expertise to include: 
 
 Design, development, integration, installation, and testing of new functionalities incorporated into the LCS trainers.

 Providing LCS trainer support (hardware, software, documentation) as required to retain training capability throughout life cycle.

 
 

 Integrate ITTs with tech refreshed CMPTs.

 Integrate ITTs with tech refreshed Multi-Data Link Management System (MDLMS). 

 Perform modernization as required in response to TECRs.

 Enter into configuration management so all software suites are properly tracked and updated.

 Install latest version of Windows, Windows Server, and Red Hat Enterprise License (RHEL) to meet DoW Cyber directive.

 Install and integrate VSHIP 10 to be compatible with latest version of Windows.

 Convert existing scenario files to VSHIP 10. 

 Remove SPLUNK and replace with ARIA to be concurrent with the ship.

 Upgrade existing hypervisors to align with tactical Total Ship Computing Environment (TSCE) modernization solution (ESXi ver. 7 u3).

 Update After Action Review (AAR) hardware and software for mission debrief.

 Update Video Display System to operate with new Operating Systems (OS) and VSHIP 10.

 Install VSHIP 10 on Common Mission Package Trainers (CMPT) and ensure they are still functional with ITTs.

ELIGIBILITY

The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is 541512 (Computer Systems Design Services), which carries a Small Business size standard of $34.0 in millions of dollars. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 6910 (Training Aids).

SUBMISSION DETAILS

This sources sought notice is not a request for competitive proposals. It is a notice to determine if a comparable source exists and outlines the Government's intent to contract on a sole source basis with General Dynamics Mission Systems. Interested sources shall submit their written technical capabilities to provide the supplies described above. Written response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. All responses shall include Company Name, Company Address, and Company Business Size as it applies under the Small Business size standard of $34.0 in millions of dollars, and Points of Contact including name, phone number, fax number, and e-mail address. Detailed written capabilities must be submitted by email to Dr. Tina Daniels (tina.daniels4.civ@us.nay.mil) with a copy to Mrs. Cynthia Armound (cynthia.d.armound.civ@us.navy.mil) in an electronic format that is compatible with Microsoft Office 365 applications (MS Word), no later than 10 a.m. Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 02 September 2026. Verbal submissions via phone will not be honored. Information and materials submitted in response to this request WILL NOT be returned. Classified material SHALL NOT be submitted.

Command and Control (C2) is foundational to warfighting, and lessons learned from recent support to contingency operations in Ukraine and Israel, as well as threat assessments in the INDOPACOM AoR, show that the Army's current C2 information systems should be modernized to meet commanders' needs for large scale combat operations against near peer adversaries.

Current mission command systems are not mobile, intuitive, or survivable enough to easily overcome the current threat, changes in the character of warfare, and the pace of technology. As part of the Army's continuous transformation effort, initiatives are being implemented to transform how the Army operates, trains, and equips for C2 capabilities that enhance its lethality, mobility, and survivability in large-scale combat as part of the Joint Force. The Army's operational imperative is to improve systems responsibly, using innovative solutions from units and industry; at the same time, preparing for the future by ensuring the next generation of C2 systems are built on a portfolio of capabilities that effectively address emerging threats and ensure dominance over adversaries.

The Army's Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) portfolio of capabilities will provide commanders with the ability to make more, better, and faster decisions through advanced analytics, an integrated data layer, open architecture, and robust and resilient transport. The result is data-centric C2 at every echelon that can operate in any environment. NGC2 requirements are currently being informed by persistent experimentation. Market research and prototyping will create a competitive environment for innovative industry partnerships and continuous integration of new technologies.

Army Contracting Command- Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG) in support of the Program Executive Office Command, Control, Communications and Network (PEO C3N) and the Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) program is publishing this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), W15P7T-25-S-0001, in accordance with the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement Subpart 212.70 for the purpose of establishing a streamlined vehicle to award innovative C2 capability and functionality.

notices.title: JOMIS Joint Medical Planning, Modeling and Simulation Capabilities
notices.agency_path: DEPT OF DEFENSE.DEFENSE HEALTH AGENCY (DHA).DEFENSE HEALTH AGENCY
notices.description_text:
Overview

The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), on behalf of the Program Executive Office Defense Healthcare Management Systems (PEO DHMS) Joint Operational Medicine Information System (JOMIS) Program Management Office (PMO), is conducting market research to inform acquisition planning for the modernization of joint medical planning capabilities.

The JOMIS PMO requires a modernized, cloud-capable, and joint-interoperable solution for efficient, adequate, and reliable medical modeling and simulation. This capability must support the development of realistic, scenario-based estimates to satisfy baseline requirements for survivability, patient safety, and quality of care during major combat operations, such as anticipated Large-Scale Combat Operations (LSCO), Defense Support of Civil Authorities (DSCA), Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) missions, and multi-domain operations below the threshold of conflict.

High-Level Objectives:

The Government is seeking innovative industry solutions to modernize and replace its legacy Joint Medical Planning Tool (JMPT) and Medical Planners Toolkit (MPTk) applications. Key areas of interest for the modernized capability include:

 
 End-to-End Casualty Continuum Modeling: Dynamic simulation of the patient pathway from Outside the Contiguous United States (OCONUS) Point of Injury (POI) through definitive Contiguous United States (CONUS) treatment and Return to Duty (RTD).

 

 
 Stochastic Logistics Projections: Moving beyond static, historical averages to calculate real-world Class VIIIA (Medical Materiel) and VIIIB (Blood) consumption rates and local stockout risks.

 

 
 Dynamic Physiological Deterioration: Modeling the progression of clinical trauma (e.g., hemorrhage, sepsis) over time, particularly under prolonged field care constraints.

 

 
 Multi-Domain and DDIL Operations: Ensuring full system operational capability in Disconnected, Disrupted, Intermittent, and Low-bandwidth (DDIL) environments with robust database synchronization and conflict resolution.

 

 
 Interoperability and Data Ingestion: Seamless integration and normalization of disparate data formats from existing Joint, Service-specific, and multinational/coalition systems, including modern Electronic Health Record (EHR) data.

 

 
 Security & Authority to Operate (ATO): Alignment with DoD Impact Level 5/6 (IL5/IL6) environments, Continuous ATO (c-ATO) pathways, and RMF cybersecurity protocols.

 

Submission Instructions:

This RFI seeks industry feedback on the attached Request for Information (RFI) Document to inform upcoming acquisition strategy decisions and requirements formulation.

 
 Maximum Page Limit: 15 Pages (excluding company profile sections).

 

 
 Proprietary Information: Any proprietary information submitted must be clearly marked. Respondents must explicitly grant permission for the Government's designated contractor support personnel to review the submitted materials.

 

 
 Submittal Deadline: Responses must be submitted electronically via email to Domonique Holmes at Domonique.p.holmes.civ@health.mil and Beth Ruckwardt at Elizabeth.m.ruckardt.civ@health.mil no later than September 13, 2026, at 1500 Eastern Time.

 

This notice is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, Invitation for Bid, Request for Proposal, or a commitment by the Government to contract. Participation is completely voluntary, and the Government will not compensate respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting responses to this RFI.

notices.description_text:
AMENDED 08/17/2026: This notice is amended to change the response date to 09/30/2026.

U.S. DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY

OFFICE OF TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE

Information Technology Manager

The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Technical Assistance (OTA) supports the development of strong financial sectors and sound public financial management in countries where assistance is needed and there is a strong commitment to reform. OTA provides technical assistance in over 50 countries in five functional areas: economic crimes, government debt and infrastructure finance, budget and financial accountability, banking and financial services, and revenue administration.

OTA is seeking an Information Technology (IT) Manager to provide a wide range of IT management and administrative services in support of its global projects. The person selected will be hired under a personal services contract. This position is located at OTA headquarters in Washington, DC. This is not a remote position. Some travel may be required.

Qualifications:

 Significant, proven working experience as an IT manager or relevant experience successfully implementing IT strategies and IT security policies, preferably in the public sector

 Technical management experience in computer networks and hardware and software systems

 Expert knowledge of information technology standards and practices to include:
 
 knowledge of IT applications and systems (e.g. operating systems and user interfaces)

 experience implementing new technologies and evaluating implemented technologies

 experience in preparing and testing disaster recovery and business continuity plan

 experience in developing, implementing and enforcing information security and control framework, policy and procedures

 
 

 Excellent written and oral communication skills

 Strong organizational skills and significant project management experience

 Proven experience in strategic planning, risk management, change management and people management

 B.S. in Computer Science, Information Systems, or related field is desired

Responsibilities and Duties:

 Provide oversight, coordination, consultation, and guidance on all IT matters and operations

 Advise management on IT issues

 Create, maintain, monitor and evaluate IT strategy and work plan, including system and functional requirements and implementation timetable

 Establish and maintain a positive working relationship with partner offices and stakeholders

 Perform IT project oversight and management, including task planning coordination, systems engineering and configuration management oversight, IT solutions validation, and IT product integrity verification

 Review and advise management on IT project cost and time estimates, application and hardware quotes, schedules and contingency plans

 Provide guidance and training to non-IT staff on IT-related systems

 Develop internal information management policies and procedures

 Advise leadership on IT capabilities and resource utilization

 Develop and manage IT budget, contractual services, and equipment, ensuring contracts are compliant with Federal regulations and agency requirements.

Please note: This is a PERSONAL SERVICES CONTRACTOR position; NOT a civil service position.

U.S. citizenship is required.

SALARY: In accordance with program regulations and based on demonstrated salary history, the current hourly rate is from $68.96 to $94.49 per hour.

BACKGROUND CHECKS AND SECURITY CLEARANCE: SECRET

Candidates will need to be eligible to obtain and maintain secret security clearance.

HOW TO APPLY: Applicants (individuals) should submit a cover letter and resume by e-mail to: recruitment@ota.treas.gov. Companies should not submit resumes on behalf of individuals. For consideration, emailed applications must not be sent, or contain a cc, to any other OTA, IRS, or other government personnel or email address.

When e-mailing, the subject line must contain the following: Solicitation 2032K826R00020 – IT Manager – Applicant's Last Name, First Name. Emails received not containing this subject line will be deemed non-responsive and will not be forwarded to selection official(s) for consideration.

No phone calls please and no hand carries. Only applicants to be interviewed will be contacted. This announcement is open and continuous through September 30, 2026, although selections may be made in advance of that date. 

Please be advised that all contractors, if hired, must obtain a Unique Entity Identifier and must maintain SAM registration.

U.S. Government is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
